bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第212卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 212
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 212

sentences.zh: 卷第二百一十二

translations.literal: Volume 212
translations.idiomatic: Volume Two Hundred Twelve

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十八】 起著雍敦牂，盡旃蒙赤奮若，凡八年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records Twenty-Eight] Beginning with Zheyong Dunzhang, ending with Zhanmeng Chifenruo, eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records, Twenty-Eight] spans from the year Zheyong-Dunzhang through Zhanmeng-Chifenruo—a period of eight years.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑，突厥毘伽可汗來請和；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinchou, the Türk Bilge Qaghan came to request peace;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's xinchou day, the Türk qaghan Bilge came seeking peace;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: [The court] granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 廣州吏民為宋璟立遺愛碑。

translations.literal: The officials and people of Guangzhou erected for Song Jing a stele commemorating his benevolent legacy.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and commoners of Guangzhou set up a stele praising Song Jing's kindness after he left office.

sentences.zh: 璟上言：「臣在州無它異跡，今以臣光寵，成彼謅諛；

translations.literal: Jing submitted a memorial, saying, "While I was in the prefecture I had no other remarkable deeds; now, because of my glory and favor, they have produced this flattery;
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing memorialized the throne: "I did nothing extraordinary as prefect, yet because of the honor now shown me they have turned to empty praise;

sentences.zh: 欲革此風，望自臣始，請敕下禁止。」

translations.literal: wishing to reform this custom, I hope it may begin with me—please issue an edict forbidding it."
translations.idiomatic: if we mean to change this habit, let it start with me—I ask that Your Majesty issue an edict forbidding such monuments."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 於是它州皆不敢立。

translations.literal: Thereupon the other prefectures all did not dare to erect [such steles].
translations.idiomatic: After that, no other prefecture dared erect one.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，敕禁惡錢，重二銖四分以上乃得行。

translations.literal: On xinyou, an edict forbade debased coin; only those weighing two zhu and four fen or more might circulate.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the court banned debased cash—only coins weighing at least two zhu and four fen could remain in circulation.

sentences.zh: 斂人間惡錢熔之，更鑄如式錢。

translations.literal: It collected debased coin from among the people, melted it down, and recoined standard money.
translations.idiomatic: The government gathered bad coin from the populace, melted it, and recast lawful currency.

sentences.zh: 於是京城紛然，賣買殆絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon the capital was in an uproar, and buying and selling nearly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The capital fell into confusion, and trade all but stopped.

sentences.zh: 宋璟、蘇頲請出太府錢二萬緡置南北方，以平價買百姓不售之物可充官用者，及聽兩京百官豫假俸錢，庶使良錢流布人間；

translations.literal: Song Jing and Su Ting requested that twenty thousand strings of cash from the Imperial Treasury be placed in the southern and northern markets to buy at fair price goods the people could not sell that might serve official needs, and that officials of the two capitals be allowed to draw their salaries in advance, so that good coin might circulate among the people;
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and Su Ting asked that twenty thousand strings from the Imperial Treasury be set aside in the northern and southern markets to purchase at fair prices unsold goods the people could spare for government use, and that officials in both capitals be allowed to draw their salaries early, so sound coin would flow back into daily use;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊子，移蔚州橫野軍於山北，屯兵三萬，為九姓之援；

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuzi, the Hengye Army of Weizhou was moved north of the mountains; thirty thousand troops were stationed there as a support for the Nine Surnames;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuzi, the court relocated the Hengye Army from Weizhou to the north side of the mountains and posted thirty thousand men there to back the Nine Surnames;

sentences.zh: 以拔曳固都督頡質略、同羅都督毘伽末啜、□都督比言、回紇都督夷健頡利發、僕固都督曳勒歌等各出騎兵為前、後、左、右軍討擊大使，皆受天兵軍節度。

translations.literal: Bayegu commander-in-chief Jiezhilüe, Tongluo commander-in-chief Bigamocho, Xi commander-in-chief Biyan, Uyghur commander-in-chief Yijian Jielifa, and Pugu commander-in-chief Yilege were each to lead cavalry as front, rear, left, and right punitive commissioners, all subject to the command of the Heavenly Troops Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhilüe, commander-in-chief of the Bayegu; Bigamocho of the Tongluo; Biyan of the Xi; Yijian Jielifa of the Uyghur; and Yilege of the Pugu were each to raise horsemen as punitive commissioners for the front, rear, left, and right wings, all under the Heavenly Troops Army.

sentences.zh: 有所討捕，量宜追集；

translations.literal: When there was pursuit and capture, they were to assemble as appropriate;
translations.idiomatic: When campaigns required it, they were to gather as needed;

sentences.zh: 無事各歸部落營生，仍常加存撫。

translations.literal: when there was no business each returned to his tribe to make a living, while they were still regularly shown care and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: in peacetime each band returned to its pastures, while the court continued to watch over them.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙巳，征嵩山處士盧鴻入見，拜諫議大夫；

translations.literal: In the third month, on yisi, the reclusive scholar Lu Hong of Mount Song was summoned to audience and appointed Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yisi, the hermit Lu Hong of Mount Song was called to court and made Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master;

sentences.zh: 鴻固辭。

translations.literal: Hong firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Hong firmly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 天兵軍使張嘉貞入朝，有告其在軍奢僭及贓賄者，按驗無狀；

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen, commissioner of the Heavenly Troops Army, came to court; someone reported that in the army he had been extravagant and usurping rank and had taken bribes—on investigation there was no substance;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen, commissioner of the Heavenly Troops Army, came to court; someone accused him of luxury, overstepping his station, and bribery while in the field, but the inquiry found nothing;

sentences.zh: 上欲反坐告者，嘉貞奏曰：「今若罪之，恐塞言路，使天下之事無由上達，願特赦之。」

translations.literal: the emperor wished to punish the accuser in turn; Jiazhen submitted, saying, "If we punish him now, I fear the path of speech will be blocked and affairs of the realm will have no way to reach Your Majesty—I beg a special pardon."
translations.idiomatic: the emperor meant to punish the accuser in turn, but Jiazhen said, "If we punish him now, we may choke off honest reports and leave Your Majesty blind to the realm—I ask that he be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 其人遂得減死。

translations.literal: That man thereupon had his death sentence reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The accuser was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 上由是以嘉貞為忠，有大用之意。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon took Jiazhen to be loyal and had the intention of giving him great employment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then judged Jiazhen loyal and began to think of promoting him to greater office.

sentences.zh: 有薦山人范知璿文學者，並獻其所為文，宋璟判之曰：「觀其《良宰論》，頗涉佞諛。

translations.literal: Someone recommended the mountain recluse Fan Zhiluan for literary talent and presented his writings together; Song Jing judged them, saying, "Judging from his 'Discourse on the Good Minister,' it rather touches on flattery and sycophancy.
translations.idiomatic: Someone recommended the recluse Fan Zhiluan for his learning and submitted his writings; Song Jing ruled, "In his 'On the Good Minister' I see more flattery than truth.

sentences.zh: 山人當極言讜議，豈宜偷合苟容！

translations.literal: A mountain recluse ought to speak out with blunt counsel—how can he fawn and seek easy acceptance!
translations.idiomatic: A man of the hills should speak blunt counsel—he ought not fawn for favor!

sentences.zh: 文章若高，自宜從選舉求試，不可別奏。」

translations.literal: If his writing is truly lofty, he should seek examination through the regular selection—he must not be presented by a separate memorial."
translations.idiomatic: If his writing is truly fine, let him enter through the regular examinations—not by a special petition."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊子，河南參軍鄭銑、朱陽丞郭仙舟投匭獻詩，敕曰：「觀其文理，乃崇道法；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuzi, Henan staff officer Zheng Xian and Zhuyang assistant magistrate Guo Xianzhou submitted poems through the suggestion box; an edict said, "Judging from the style and reasoning, they honor the Way and its methods;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wuzi, Zheng Xian, a staff officer of Henan, and Guo Xianzhou, assistant magistrate of Zhuyang, dropped poems into the suggestion box; the emperor replied, "Their style shows devotion to the Way;

sentences.zh: 至於時用，不切事情。

translations.literal: as for present utility, they do not fit the affairs at hand.
translations.idiomatic: but for practical governance they miss the mark.

sentences.zh: 宜各從所好。」

translations.literal: Each should follow his own preference."
translations.idiomatic: Let each follow his own bent."

sentences.zh: 並罷官，度為道士。

translations.literal: Both were dismissed from office and ordained as Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: Both were removed from office and ordained as Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛亥，以突騎施都督蘇祿為左羽林大將軍、順國公，充金方道經略大使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on xinhai, Turgesh commander-in-chief Suolu was made Left General of the Feathered Forest, Duke of Shunguo, and served as commissioner for the Jinfang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinhai, Suolu, commander-in-chief of the Turgesh, was appointed Left General of the Feathered Forest, made Duke of Shunguo, and named commissioner for the Jinfang circuit.

sentences.zh: 契丹王李失活卒，癸巳，以其弟娑固代之。

translations.literal: Khitan king Li Shihuo died; on guisi his younger brother Suogu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan king Li Shihuo died; on guisi his younger brother Suogu took the throne.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，頒鄉飲酒禮於州縣，令每歲十二月行之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, the village drinking ceremony was promulgated to prefectures and counties, ordering it to be performed every twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, the court extended the village drinking rite to every prefecture and county, to be held each twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 唐初，州縣官俸，皆令富戶掌錢，出息以給之；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, prefectural and county officials' salaries were all entrusted to wealthy households to hold the funds and pay interest to supply them;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang, local officials' salaries were funded by wealthy households who held public funds and paid interest on them;

sentences.zh: 息至倍稱，多破產者。

translations.literal: interest reached double the principal, and many went bankrupt.
translations.idiomatic: interest often doubled the principal, ruining many families.

sentences.zh: 秘書少監崔沔上言，請計州縣官所得俸，於百姓常賦之外，微有所加以給之。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Secretariat Cui Mian submitted a memorial requesting that the salaries received by prefectural and county officials be calculated and that, beyond the people's regular taxes, a slight addition be levied to pay them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mian, Assistant Director of the Secretariat, proposed calculating officials' salaries and funding them with a small surcharge beyond the regular tax.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，辛卯，車駕至西京。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on xinmao, the imperial carriage arrived at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on xinmao, the emperor reached the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，吐蕃奉表請和，乞舅甥親署誓文，及令彼此宰相皆著名於其上。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Tibet submitted a memorial requesting peace, asking that the uncle and nephew personally sign the oath text and that the chief ministers of both sides affix their names upon it.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Tibet petitioned for peace, asking that the emperor and the Tibetan ruler sign the treaty as uncle and nephew and that ministers on both sides add their names.

sentences.zh: 宋璟奏：「括州員外司馬李邕、儀州司馬鄭勉，並有才略文詞，但性多異端，好是非改變；

translations.literal: Song Jing submitted: "Kuozhou supernumerary aide Li Yong and Yizhou aide Zheng Mian both have talent, strategy, and literary skill, but their natures are full of unorthodox ways and they delight in stirring up right and wrong and making changes;
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing reported: "Li Yong, supernumerary aide of Kuozhou, and Zheng Mian, aide of Yizhou, are both gifted in policy and letters, yet they are restless, fond of faction, and prone to overturn settled matters;

sentences.zh: 若全引進，則咎悔必至，若長棄捐，則才用可惜，請除渝、硤二州剌史。」

translations.literal: if they are fully brought forward, blame and regret are sure to come; if they are long cast aside, their talent would be a pity—please appoint them prefects of Yu and Xia."
translations.idiomatic: if we promote them fully, trouble will follow; if we discard them forever, we waste their gifts—appoint them prefects of Yu and Xia instead."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「大理卿元行沖素稱才行，初用之時，實允僉議；

translations.literal: He also submitted: "Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Xingchong has long been praised for ability and conduct; when first appointed, he truly met with general approval;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Yuan Xingchong, Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, has long been praised for ability; at first everyone approved his appointment;

sentences.zh: 當事之後，頗非稱積，請復以為左散騎常侍，以李朝隱代之。

translations.literal: after handling affairs, his accumulated reputation has been rather poor—please restore him as Left Regular Attendant and have Li Chaoyin replace him.
translations.idiomatic: in office his record has fallen short—restore him to Left Regular Attendant and let Li Chaoyin take his place as judge.

sentences.zh: 陸象先閒於政體，寬不容非，請以為河南尹。」

translations.literal: Lu Xiangxian is versed in the forms of government, broad-minded and not fault-finding—please make him Intendant of Henan."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangxian understands governance, is broad-minded and slow to blame—make him Intendant of Henan."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，俱密王那羅延、康王烏勒伽、安王篤薩波提皆上表言為大食所侵掠，乞兵救援。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, Jumi king Narayan, Kang king Wulejia, and An king Dusaboti all submitted memorials saying they had been invaded and plundered by the Arabs and begged troops for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, King Narayan of Jumi, King Wulejia of Kang, and King Dusaboti of An all petitioned that Arab forces were raiding them and asked for military aid.

sentences.zh: 敕太府及府縣出粟十萬石糶之，以斂人間惡錢，送少府銷毀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Imperial Granary and prefectures and counties to release one hundred thousand piculs of grain for sale, to gather debased coin from among the people and send it to the Palace Workshops for destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Imperial Granary and local governments to sell one hundred thousand piculs of grain, gather bad coin from the people, and send it to the Palace Workshops to be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙卯，以左武衛大將軍、檢校內外閒廄使、苑內營田使王毛仲行太僕卿。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yimao, Left Martial Guard General, acting commissioner of the inner and outer stud farms, and commissioner of farming within the imperial park Wang Maoqian was made acting Grand Master of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yimao, Wang Maoqian—Left Martial Guard General, acting commissioner of the inner and outer stud farms, and overseer of park agriculture—was appointed acting Grand Master of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 毛仲嚴察有干力，萬騎功臣、閒廄官吏皆憚之，苑內所收常豐溢。

translations.literal: Maoqian was strict in inspection and had practical ability; the Ten Thousand Cavalry meritocrats and stud officials all feared him, and what the park collected was always abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqian was severe and capable; the Ten Thousand Cavalry veterans and stud officials all feared him, and the imperial parks always yielded a surplus.

sentences.zh: 上以為能，故有寵。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him capable and therefore favored him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took him for able and favored him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 雖有外第，常居閒廄側內宅，上或時不見，則悄然若有所失；

translations.literal: Although he had an outer mansion, he usually lived in the inner residence beside the stud; when the emperor did not see him for a time, he would grow quietly as though he had lost something;
translations.idiomatic: Though he had a house outside the palace, he usually stayed in the inner quarters by the stud; if the emperor went days without seeing him, the emperor grew restless as though something were missing;

sentences.zh: 宦官楊思勖、高力士皆畏避之。

translations.literal: the eunuchs Yang Sixun and Gao Lishi all feared and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: even the eunuchs Yang Sixun and Gao Lishi kept their distance out of fear.

sentences.zh: 渤海王大祚榮卒；

translations.literal: Bohai king Da Zuorong died;
translations.idiomatic: Da Zuorong, king of Bohai, died;

sentences.zh: 丙辰，命其子武藝襲位。

translations.literal: on bingchen his son Wuyi was ordered to succeed to the position.
translations.idiomatic: on bingchen the court recognized his son Wuyi as successor.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬午，開府儀同三司祁公王仁皎薨。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renwu, Qi Duke Wang Renjiao, Grand Master of the Palace with the Honor of the Three Excellencies, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renwu, Wang Renjiao, Duke of Qi and Grand Master of the Palace with the Honor of the Three Excellencies, died.

sentences.zh: 其子駙馬都尉守一請用竇孝諶例，築墳高五丈一尺；

translations.literal: His son, Commandant of the Horse for the Imperial Son-in-law Shouyi, requested to follow the precedent of Dou Xiaochen and build the tomb mound fifty-one chi high;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouyi, an imperial son-in-law, asked—following the precedent of Dou Xiaochen—to raise a mound fifty-one chi high;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 宋璟、蘇頲固爭，以為：「准令，一品墳高一丈九尺，其陪陵者高出三丈而已。

translations.literal: Song Jing and Su Ting firmly remonstrated, saying, "According to the statutes, a first-rank tomb is one zhang and nine chi high; for those buried as companions to the imperial tombs, exceeding three zhang is all that is allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and Su Ting protested firmly: "Statute sets a first-rank tomb at one zhang nine chi; even for those buried near the imperial tombs, three zhang is the limit.

sentences.zh: 竇太尉墳，議者頗譏其高大，當時無人極言其失，豈可今日復踵而為之！

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Dou's tomb was widely criticized by discussants as too lofty; at the time no one spoke out fully against the fault—how can we today follow in his footsteps again!
translations.idiomatic: Dou the Grand Marshal's mound was already mocked as too tall, and no one then dared speak plainly—how can we repeat that mistake today!

sentences.zh: 昔太宗嫁女，資送過於長公主。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Taizong married off a daughter, the dowry exceeded that of the eldest imperial princess.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong married off a daughter, her dowry outdid the eldest princess's.

sentences.zh: 魏徵進諫，太宗既用其言，文德皇后亦賞之。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated; Taizong both adopted his words, and Empress Wende also praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated; Taizong took his advice, and Empress Wende praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 豈若韋庶人崇其父墳，號曰酆陵，以自速其禍乎！

translations.literal: How was that like Consort Wei glorifying her father's tomb, calling it Fengling, and thereby hastening her own disaster!
translations.idiomatic: That was nothing like Consort Wei, who glorified her father's tomb as Fengling and brought ruin on herself!

sentences.zh: 夫以後父之尊，欲高大其墳，何足為難！

translations.literal: For one in the honored position of an empress's father, wishing to make his tomb lofty—what difficulty is there in that!
translations.idiomatic: For an empress's father, raising a grand tomb is easy enough!

sentences.zh: 而臣等再三進言者，蓋欲成中宮之美耳。

translations.literal: Yet the reason we ministers speak again and again is simply that we wish to complete the empress's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: We speak again and again only to preserve the empress's good name.

sentences.zh: 況今日所為，當傳無窮，永以為法，可不慎乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, what is done today will be transmitted without end and taken as law forever—can we not be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: What you do today will become precedent forever—can you not be careful!"

sentences.zh: 上悅曰：「朕每欲正身率下，況於妻子，何敢私之！

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure, "I always wish to correct my person and lead those below; how much more for wife and children—how would I dare show favoritism!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said gladly, "I mean to set an example for the realm—how could I favor my own wife and kin!

sentences.zh: 然此乃人所難言，卿能固守典禮，以成朕美，垂法將來，誠所望也。」

translations.literal: Yet this is what others find hard to say; that you can hold fast to the canonical rites, complete my virtue, and hand down a law to the future is truly what I hope for."
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is hard counsel to give; that you hold to ritual, complete my reputation, and set a standard for posterity is exactly what I want."

sentences.zh: 賜璟、頲帛四百匹。

translations.literal: He bestowed four hundred bolts of silk on Jing and Ting.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Jing and Ting with four hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day yichou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the new moon of yichou, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 上素服以俟變，徹樂減膳，命中書、門下察系囚，賑饑乏，勸農功。

translations.literal: The emperor wore plain dress to await the change, withdrew music and reduced meals, and ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to examine prisoners in custody, relieve hunger and want, and encourage agricultural work.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore plain robes, halted music, cut his meals, and ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to review prisoners, aid the hungry, and promote farming.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，宋璟等奏曰：「陛下勤恤人隱，此誠蒼生之福。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Song Jing and others submitted, saying, "Your Majesty diligently cares for the people's hidden suffering—this is truly the common people's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Song Jing and others said, "Your Majesty's care for the people's hardships is a blessing to the realm.

sentences.zh: 然臣聞日食修德，月食修刑；

translations.literal: Yet we have heard that for a solar eclipse one cultivates virtue, and for a lunar eclipse one reforms punishments;
translations.idiomatic: Yet we are taught that a solar eclipse calls for cultivating virtue, a lunar eclipse for reforming punishments;

sentences.zh: 親君子，遠小人，絕女謁，除讒慝，所謂修德也。

translations.literal: being close to gentlemen, keeping petty men at a distance, cutting off women's access, and removing slanderous villains—this is what is called cultivating virtue.
translations.idiomatic: drawing near the worthy, keeping petty men at bay, shutting palace women's influence, and rooting out slander—that is true virtue.

sentences.zh: 君子恥言浮於行，苟推至誠以行之，不必數下制書也。」

translations.literal: A gentleman is ashamed when words exceed deeds; if Your Majesty would push utmost sincerity in acting, there is no need repeatedly to issue edicts."
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman is ashamed when words outrun deeds; act with utmost sincerity, and there is no need for repeated edicts."

sentences.zh: 六月，戊辰，吐蕃復遣使請上親署誓文；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuchen, Tibet again sent envoys requesting that the emperor personally sign the oath text;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuchen, Tibet again asked that the emperor sign the treaty in person;

sentences.zh: 上不許，曰：「昔歲誓約已定，苟信不由衷，亟誓何益！」

translations.literal: the emperor did not grant it, saying, "Last year's sworn covenant is already settled; if good faith does not come from the heart, what use is swearing again and again!"
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused, saying, "Last year's oath is already set; if faith is not sincere, what good is another treaty!"

sentences.zh: 秋，閏七月，右補闕盧履冰上言：「禮，父在為母服週年，則天皇后改服齊衰三年，請復其舊。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the intercalary seventh month, Right Remonstrance and Consultation Official Lu Lübing submitted, saying, "According to ritual, while the father lives one wears mourning for the mother for one year; Empress Zetian changed it to three years of qi and cui mourning—please restore the old rule."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the intercalary seventh month, Lu Lübing, Right Remonstrance and Consultation Official, said, "Ritual requires one year of mourning for a mother while the father lives; Empress Wu extended it to three years—please restore the ancient rule."

sentences.zh: 上下其議。

translations.literal: The matter was sent up and down for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The court referred the matter for debate.

sentences.zh: 左散騎常侍褚無量以履冰議為是；

translations.literal: Left Regular Attendant Chu Wuliang held Lübing's proposal to be correct;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Wuliang, Left Regular Attendant, sided with Lübing;

sentences.zh: 諸人爭論，連年不決。

translations.literal: the various men argued, and for successive years no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: others disputed the point, and for years no settlement was reached.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛卯，敕自今五服並依《喪服傳》文，然士大夫議論猶不息，行之各從其意。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinmao, an edict ordered that from now on the five grades of mourning all follow the text of the Classic of Mourning Dress, yet the gentry and officials' discussions still did not cease, and in practice each followed his own inclination.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinmao, an edict declared that henceforth all five grades of mourning would follow the Classic of Mourning Dress, yet scholars kept arguing, and in practice each household did as it pleased.

sentences.zh: 無量歎曰：「聖人豈不知母恩之厚乎？

translations.literal: Wuliang sighed and said, "Do the sages not know how deep a mother's kindness is?
translations.idiomatic: Chu Wuliang sighed, "Do the sages not know a mother's love?

sentences.zh: 厭降之禮，所以明尊卑、異戎狄也。

translations.literal: The rite of diminishing and lowering is precisely to clarify honor and baseness and to distinguish from the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The rite that lowers mourning for a mother is meant to mark rank and set us apart from barbarians.

sentences.zh: 俗情膚淺，不知聖人之心，一紊其制，誰能正之！」

translations.literal: Popular feeling is shallow and does not know the sages' hearts; once the system is thrown into disorder, who can set it right!"
translations.idiomatic: The vulgar are shallow and miss the sages' intent; once custom is confused, who can restore it!"

sentences.zh: 九月，甲寅，徙宋王憲為寧王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiayin, Prince Song Xian was moved to be Prince Ning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiayin, Prince Song Xian was renamed Prince of Ning.

sentences.zh: 上嘗從復道中見衛士食畢，棄餘食於竇中，怒，欲杖殺之；

translations.literal: The emperor once, from a covered passage, saw guards after eating discard leftover food into a drain; in anger he wished to beat them to death;
translations.idiomatic: Once, watching from a covered passage, the emperor saw guards throw leftover food into a drain after their meal; enraged, he meant to beat them to death;

sentences.zh: 左右莫敢言。

translations.literal: those at his side did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: no one at his side dared speak.

sentences.zh: 憲從容諫曰：「陛下從復道中窺人過失而殺之，臣恐人人不自安。

translations.literal: Xian calmly remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty, peering from a covered passage at others' faults and killing them for them—I fear everyone will be ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said calmly, "If Your Majesty spies on men's faults from hidden passages and kills them for it, I fear no one will feel safe.

sentences.zh: 且陛下惡棄食於地者，為食可以養人也；

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty hates discarding food on the ground because food can nourish people;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you hate wasted food because food nourishes people;

sentences.zh: 今以餘食殺人，無乃失其本乎！」

translations.literal: now to kill a man over leftover food—are we not losing the root of the matter!"
translations.idiomatic: yet now you would kill a man over scraps—have you not lost the point!"

sentences.zh: 上大悟，蹶然起曰：「微兄，幾至濫刑。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enlightened, started up abruptly, and said, "Without you, elder brother, I would nearly have reached abusive punishment."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to himself, rose abruptly, and said, "Without you, brother, I would have committed a grave abuse."

sentences.zh: 遽釋衛士。

translations.literal: He at once released the guards.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately released the guards.

sentences.zh: 是日，上宴飲極歡，自解紅玉帶，並所乘馬以賜憲。

translations.literal: That day the emperor feasted and drank with the utmost joy, and himself unfastened his red jade belt and also the horse he rode to bestow them on Xian.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor feasted in high spirits and gave Xian his own red jade belt and the horse he had ridden.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛卯，上幸驪山溫湯；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinmao, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinmao, the emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 癸卯，還宮。

translations.literal: On guimao, [the emperor] returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 壬子，冊拜突騎施蘇祿為忠順可汗。

translations.literal: On renzi, [the court] invested by patent Sulu of the Turgesh as the Loyal and Obedient Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the emperor invested Sulu of the Turgesh as Loyal and Obedient Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬申，契丹王李娑固與公主入朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renshen, the Khitan king Li Suogu and the princess came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renshen, Khitan king Li Suogu and the princess presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 上以岐山令王仁琛，籓邸故吏，墨敕令與五品官。

translations.literal: The emperor, [regarding] Wang Renchen, magistrate of Qishan—a former clerk from his princely residence—issued an ink edict granting him a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had issued an informal ink edict making Wang Renchen, magistrate of Qishan and once a clerk in his princely household, a fifth-rank official.

sentences.zh: 宋璟奏：「故舊恩私，則有大例，除官資歷，非無公道。

translations.literal: Song Jing submitted, saying, "Favoritism for old friends and personal ties has broad precedents, but appointment according to official qualification and service record is not without public principle.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing memorialized: "There is ample precedent for showing kindness to old friends, yet appointments must still follow rank and seniority—that is what fairness demands.

sentences.zh: 仁琛向緣舊恩，已獲優改，今若再蒙超獎，遂於諸人不類；

translations.literal: Renchen, relying on former favor, has already received preferential promotion; if he were now again to receive exceptional reward, it would no longer be of a kind with the others;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renchen has already benefited once from past favor; to shower him with another extraordinary promotion would set him apart from everyone else—

sentences.zh: 又是後族，須杜輿言。

translations.literal: moreover he is of the empress's kindred—we must stop wagging tongues.
translations.idiomatic: and as a relative of the empress, we must silence gossip.

sentences.zh: 乞下吏部檢勘，苟無負犯，於格應留，請依資稍優注擬。」

translations.literal: I beg that the Ministry of Personnel be ordered to examine [his record]; if he has no offenses on his record and by regulation ought to be retained, please assign him a post with slight preference according to seniority."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Ministry of Personnel review his record—if it is clean and he qualifies for retention, let him be posted with only a modest advantage in seniority."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 選人宋元超於吏部自言侍中璟之叔父，冀得優假。

translations.literal: The examination candidate Song Yuanchao declared at the Ministry of Personnel that he was Palace Attendant Jing's uncle, hoping to receive preferential leniency.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Personnel, examination candidate Song Yuanchao identified himself as Palace Attendant Song Jing's uncle, hoping for special favor.

sentences.zh: 璟聞之，牒吏部云：「元超，璟之三從叔，常在洛城，不多參見。

translations.literal: When Jing heard of this, he sent a note to the Ministry of Personnel, saying, "Yuanchao is Jing's third cousin once removed; he has long lived in Luoyang and I have seldom seen him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing learned of this, he wrote to the Ministry: "Yuanchao is my third cousin once removed. He has lived in Luoyang for years and I rarely see him.

sentences.zh: 既不敢緣尊輒隱，又不願以私害公。

translations.literal: I dare not, because of senior kinship, simply conceal this; nor do I wish private feeling to harm the public good.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot stay silent out of family rank, but I will not let private ties corrupt public duty either.

sentences.zh: 向者無言，自依大例，既有聲聽，事須矯枉；

translations.literal: Before, when nothing was said, he naturally followed the general rule; now that his claim has become known, the matter must be set straight;
translations.idiomatic: When no one had heard of his claim, ordinary rules were enough; now that word has spread, we must correct the error—

sentences.zh: 請放。」

translations.literal: I request his dismissal [from candidacy]."
translations.idiomatic: please reject his candidacy."

sentences.zh: 寧王憲奏選人薛嗣先請授微官，事下中書、門下。

translations.literal: Prince of Ning Xian submitted that the examination candidate Xue Sixian requested appointment to a minor office; the matter was referred to the Central Secretariat and the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning Xian recommended candidate Xue Sixian for a minor post, and the case went to the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 璟奏：「嗣先兩選齋郎，雖非灼然應留，以懿親之故，固應微假官資。

translations.literal: Jing submitted, saying, "Sixian has twice served as Libationer through examination; though he is not clearly eligible for retention, because of close imperial kinship he certainly ought to receive slight leniency in official qualification.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing replied: "Sixian twice passed as a libationer. He does not clearly qualify for retention, but as close imperial kin he may deserve modest favor in rank—

sentences.zh: 在景龍中，常有墨敕處分，謂之斜封。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era there were often ink-edict dispositions, called 'slant-seal' appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jinglong reign, such favors came by ink edict—the so-called 'slant-seal' appointments.

sentences.zh: 自大明臨御，茲事杜絕，行一賞，命一官，必是緣功與才，皆歷中書、門下。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, this practice has been ended; every reward or appointment must be based on merit and talent, and all pass through the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession that route has been shut off—every honor and every post must rest on merit and talent, and every one passes through the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 至公之道，唯聖能行。

translations.literal: The way of utmost fairness—only a sage can carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Only a sage could uphold such absolute fairness.

sentences.zh: 嗣先幸預姻戚，不為屈法，許臣等商量，望付吏部知，不出正敕。」

translations.literal: Sixian happens to be among the marriage kin; not to bend the law, I allow us ministers to deliberate; I hope he may be referred to the Ministry of Personnel for processing, without an orthodox patent edict."
translations.idiomatic: Sixian is fortunate in his marriage ties; we need not bend the law—let us ministers discuss it and refer the matter to Personnel without a formal patent edict."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝集使往往繼貨入京師，及春將還，多遷官；

translations.literal: Previously, provincial assembly envoys often brought goods in succession to the capital; when spring came and they were about to return, many received transferred appointments;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, provincial envoys arriving for the annual assembly often loaded up goods for the capital, and many went home in spring with fresh promotions—

sentences.zh: 宋璟奏一切勒還，以革其弊。

translations.literal: Song Jing submitted that all should be ordered to return, to reform this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing proposed sending them all home at once to break the habit.

sentences.zh: 是歲，置劍南節度使，領益、彭等二十五州。

translations.literal: This year, the Jiannan military commissioner was established, governing Yi, Peng, and twenty-three other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court created the Jiannan military commissioner, with authority over Yi, Peng, and twenty-three other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙辰，左散騎常侍褚無量卒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingchen, Left Regular Attendant Chu Wuliang died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on bingchen, Left Regular Attendant Chu Wuliang died.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，命右散騎常侍元行沖整比群書。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Right Regular Attendant Yuan Xingchong was ordered to collate and compare the collected books.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the emperor charged Right Regular Attendant Yuan Xingchong with collating the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 侍中宋璟疾負罪而妄訴不已者，悉付御史台治之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Song Jing, vexed by those who bore guilt yet incessantly lodged false appeals, handed them all over to the Censorate for prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing, weary of guilty men who kept filing baseless appeals, turned them all over to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 謂中丞李謹度曰：「服不更訴者出之，尚訴未已者且系。」

translations.literal: He said to Censor-in-Chief Li Jindu, "Those who submit and lodge no further appeals—release them; those still appealing without end—detain them for now."
translations.idiomatic: He told Censor-in-Chief Li Jindu: "Release anyone who stops appealing; hold anyone who still will not stop."

sentences.zh: 由是人多怨者。

translations.literal: Thereupon many people bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment spread among many.

sentences.zh: 會天旱有魃，優人作魃狀戲於上前，問魃：「何為出？」

translations.literal: When drought brought forth a drought demon, actors costumed as the demon performed before the emperor and [someone] asked the demon, "Why have you come forth?"
translations.idiomatic: During a drought a demon was said to appear; performers dressed as it played before the emperor, who asked, "Why have you come out?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「奉相公處分。」

translations.literal: It answered, "By the chief minister's disposition."
translations.idiomatic: The reply: "At the chief minister's command."

sentences.zh: 又問：「何故？」

translations.literal: [He] asked again, "For what reason?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "Why?"

sentences.zh: 魃曰：「負冤者三百餘人，相公悉以繫獄抑之，故魃不得不出。」

translations.literal: The demon said, "More than three hundred who bear injustice—the chief minister has put them all in prison and suppressed them, so the drought demon cannot but come forth."
translations.idiomatic: The demon said, "Three hundred innocent men sit imprisoned at the chief minister's order—the drought demon had to appear."

sentences.zh: 上心以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart took this to be so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found this convincing.

sentences.zh: 時璟與中書侍郎、同平章事蘇頲建議嚴禁惡錢，江、淮間惡錢尤甚，璟以監察御史蕭隱之充使括惡錢。

translations.literal: At the time Jing and Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and Associate Counselor Su Ting proposed strictly forbidding debased coin; debased coin was especially severe between the Yangzi and Huai, and Jing appointed Supervising Censor Xiao Yinzhi as commissioner to investigate debased coin.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Song Jing and Vice Director Su Ting had pushed to ban debased coin, worst of all in the Jiang-Huai region; Jing sent Supervising Censor Xiao Yinzhi to root it out.

sentences.zh: 隱之嚴急煩擾，怨嗟盈路，上於是貶隱之官。

translations.literal: Yinzhi was harsh, urgent, vexing, and disruptive; resentment and lament filled the roads; the emperor thereupon demoted Yinzhi in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhi's campaign was fierce and intrusive; complaints filled the roads, and the emperor demoted him.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，罷璟為開府儀同三司，頲為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Jing was removed [from office] and made Grand Master of the Palace with the Honor of the Three Excellencies; Ting was made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Song Jing was stripped of office and made Grand Master of the Palace with the Honor of the Three Excellencies; Su Ting was made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以京兆尹源乾曜為黃門侍郎，并州長史張嘉貞為中書侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Capital Prefect Yuan Gan'yao was made Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Bingzhou Chief Administrator Zhang Jiazhen was made Vice Director of the Central Secretariat; both were made associate counselors.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Prefect Yuan Gan'yao became Vice Director of the Chancellery and Bingzhou chief administrator Zhang Jiazhen became Vice Director of the Secretariat; both joined the council.

sentences.zh: 於是弛錢禁，惡錢復行矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the coin prohibition was relaxed, and debased coin circulated again.
translations.idiomatic: The coin ban was lifted, and debased cash flowed again.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊戌，皇子敏卒，追立為懷王，謚曰哀。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuxu, the prince Min died; posthumously he was established as Prince Huai, with posthumous title Ai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuxu, Prince Min died and was posthumously installed as Prince Huai, posthumous name Ai ("Lamented").

sentences.zh: 壬子，敕以役莫重於軍府，一為衛士，六十乃免，宜促其歲限，使百姓更迭為之。

translations.literal: On renzi, an edict said that among corvée labor none was heavier than guard service in the army offices—once enrolled as an imperial guardsman, one was not released until sixty; [the court] should shorten this term so the common people could take turns serving.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi an edict noted that guard duty was the heaviest corvée—once drafted into the palace guard a man served until sixty. The term should be shortened so families could rotate the burden.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙午，遣使賜烏長王、骨咄王、俱位王冊命。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingwu, envoys were dispatched to bestow patent investiture on the king of Wuchang, the king of Gutu, and the king of Juwei.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingwu, the court sent envoys bearing patents to the kings of Wuchang, Gutu, and Juwei.

sentences.zh: 三國皆在大食之西，大食慾誘之叛唐，三國不從，故褒之。

translations.literal: The three states all lay west of Dashi; Dashi wished to entice them to rebel against Tang, but the three states did not comply; therefore [Tang] rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: All three kingdoms lay west of the Arabs; when the Arabs tried to turn them against Tang they refused—hence the imperial reward.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛酉，復置十道按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on xinyou, the ten-circuit investigating commissioners were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinyou, the court restored the ten-circuit investigating commissioners.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以源乾曜為侍中，張嘉貞為中書令。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Yuan Gan'yao was made Palace Attendant and Zhang Jiazhen was made Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Yuan Gan'yao became Palace Attendant and Zhang Jiazhen became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾曜上言：「形要之家多任京官，使俊乂之士沉廢於外。

translations.literal: Gan'yao submitted, saying, "Families of influence and power often hold capital offices, causing able men to languish outside [the capital].
translations.idiomatic: Gan'yao memorialized: "Powerful families crowd the capital with their sons while able men waste away in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 臣三子皆在京，請出其二人。」

translations.literal: My three sons are all in the capital; I request that two of them be sent out."
translations.idiomatic: All three of my sons serve in the capital—I ask that two be posted elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 因下制稱乾曜之公，命文武官效之，於是出者百餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued praising Gan'yao's public-mindedness and ordering civil and military officials to emulate him; thereby more than a hundred [officials' sons] were sent out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended his public spirit and urged officials to follow suit; more than a hundred sons of officials were reassigned to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞吏事強敏，而剛躁自用。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen was sharp and quick in administrative affairs, but headstrong, impatient, and self-willed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen was a sharp administrator, but rigid, hot-tempered, and obstinate.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人苗延嗣、呂太一、考功員外郎員嘉靜、殿中侍御史崔訓皆嘉貞所引進，常與之議政事。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafters Miao Yansi and Lü Taiyi, Outer Office Director of Examination Yuan Jiajing, and Palace Censor Cui Xun were all men Jiazhen had advanced; they often deliberated on state affairs with him.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafters Miao Yansi and Lü Taiyi, examination director Yuan Jiajing, and palace censor Cui Xun were all his protégés and often debated policy with him.

sentences.zh: 四人頗招權，時人語曰：「令公四俊，苗、呂、崔、員。」

translations.literal: The four men rather gathered power; people at the time said, "The Minister's four outstanding men—Miao, Lü, Cui, and Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: The four wielded considerable influence; people said, "The Minister's four bright stars—Miao, Lü, Cui, and Yuan."

sentences.zh: 六月，瀍、穀漲溢，漂溺幾二千人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Chan and Gu rivers rose and overflowed, drowning nearly two thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month floods on the Chan and Gu rivers drowned nearly two thousand people.

sentences.zh: 突厥降戶僕固都督勺磨及□夾跌部落散居受降城側，朔方大使王晙言其陰引突厥，謀陷軍城，密奏請誅之。

translations.literal: Among surrendered Türk households, Pugu Protector Shaomo and the Tiele affiliated tribes living scattered beside Shouxiang City—Shuofang Commissioner Wang Jun reported that they secretly welcomed the Türks and plotted to seize the garrison city; he secretly submitted requesting their execution.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered Türk households—the Pugu protector Shaomo and Tiele affiliated tribes scattered near Shouxiang City—were accused by Shuofang commissioner Wang Jun of secretly colluding with the Türks to storm the garrison; he secretly asked permission to kill them.

sentences.zh: 誘勺磨等宴於受降城，伏兵悉殺之，河曲降戶殆盡。

translations.literal: [Jun] lured Shaomo and the others to a banquet at Shouxiang City; concealed troops killed them all; the surrendered households of the river bend were nearly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Shaomo and the others to a banquet at Shouxiang City and had them killed by ambush; the surrendered tribes along the bend of the Yellow River were almost wiped out.

sentences.zh: 拔曳固、同羅諸部在大同、橫野軍之側者，聞之皆忷懼。

translations.literal: The Bayegu, Tongluo, and other tribes beside Datong and Hengye Garrisons, on hearing this, were all fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Bayegu, Tongluo, and other tribes camped near Datong and Hengye garrisons were terror-stricken at the news.

sentences.zh: 秋，并州長史、天兵節度大使張說引二十騎，持節即其部落慰撫之，因宿其帳下。

translations.literal: In autumn, Bingzhou Chief Administrator and Heavenly Troops Military Commissioner Zhang Yue led twenty mounted escorts, bearing credentials, went straight to their camps to console and reassure them, and lodged overnight in their tents.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Bingzhou chief administrator and Heavenly Troops commissioner Zhang Yue took twenty horsemen with imperial credentials straight to their camps to reassure them—and spent the night in their tents.

sentences.zh: 副使李憲以虜情難信，馳書止之。

translations.literal: Deputy Commissioner Li Xian, deeming the barbarians' sentiments hard to trust, sent a fast letter telling him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioner Li Xian thought the tribes could not be trusted and sent an urgent letter ordering him to turn back.

sentences.zh: 說復書曰：「吾肉非黃羊，必不畏食；

translations.literal: Yue replied by letter, saying, "My flesh is not that of a yellow sheep—I surely need not fear being eaten;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue wrote back: "My flesh is not mutton—I am not afraid it will be eaten;

sentences.zh: 血非野馬，必不畏刺。

translations.literal: my blood is not that of a wild horse—I surely need not fear being stabbed.
translations.idiomatic: my blood is not wild-horse blood—I am not afraid it will be spilled.

sentences.zh: 士見危致命，此吾效死之秋也。」

translations.literal: When a gentleman sees danger he gives his life—this is the season for me to die in service."
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman dies when duty calls—this is my moment."

sentences.zh: 拔曳固、同羅由是遂安。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bayegu and Tongluo were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Bayegu and Tongluo were reassured.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛巳，上行幸長春宮；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, the emperor proceeded to Changchun Palace;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, the emperor went to Changchun Palace;

sentences.zh: 壬午，畋於下邽。

translations.literal: on renwu, he hunted at Xia Gui.
translations.idiomatic: on renwu he hunted at Xia Gui.

sentences.zh: 上禁約諸王，不使與群臣交結。

translations.literal: The emperor restricted and warned the princes, not allowing them to form associations with officials and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor forbade the princes to cultivate ties with court officials.

sentences.zh: 光祿少卿駙馬都尉裴虛己與岐王范游宴，仍私挾讖緯；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Household and Empress's Son-in-Law Commandant Pei Xuji consorted and feasted with Prince of Qi Fan, and privately carried prognostications and weft texts;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Imperial Household and imperial son-in-law Pei Xuji caroused with Prince of Qi Fan and privately kept prophetic texts;

sentences.zh: 戊子，流虛己於新州，離其公主。

translations.literal: on wuzi, Xuji was banished to Xin Prefecture and separated from his princess.
translations.idiomatic: on wuzi Pei Xuji was exiled to Xin Prefecture and separated from his wife the princess.

sentences.zh: 萬年尉劉庭琦、太祝張諤數與范飲酒賦詩，貶庭琦雅州司戶，諤山茌丞。

translations.literal: Wannian Assistant Magistrate Liu Tingqi and Grand Supplicator Zhang E repeatedly drank and composed poetry with Fan; Tingqi was demoted to Registrar of Ya Prefecture, E to Assistant Magistrate of Shanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian assistant magistrate Liu Tingqi and grand supplicator Zhang E had often drunk and written poetry with Fan; Liu was demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture and Zhang to assistant magistrate of Shanqi.

sentences.zh: 然待范如故，謂左右曰：「吾兄弟自無間，但趨競之徒強相托附耳。

translations.literal: Yet [the emperor] treated Fan as before, saying to attendants, "Among us brothers there is no estrangement—it is only those eager to scramble who forcibly attach themselves to us.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor treated Prince Fan as before, telling attendants, "There is no rift between my brothers—only ambitious men thrust themselves upon us.

sentences.zh: 吾終不以此責兄弟也。」

translations.literal: I will never because of this blame my brothers."
translations.idiomatic: I will never hold my brothers responsible for that."

sentences.zh: 上嘗不豫，薛王業妃弟內直郎韋賓與殿中監皇甫恂私議休咎；

translations.literal: The emperor was once unwell; Inner Attendant Wei Bin, younger brother of Prince of Xue Ye's consort, and Director of the Palace Domestic Service Huangfu Xun privately discussed good and ill fortune;
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor was ill, inner attendant Wei Bin—brother of Prince of Xue Ye's consort—and palace director Huangfu Xun privately debated the omen;

sentences.zh: 事覺，賓杖死，恂貶錦州刺史。

translations.literal: when the matter came to light, Bin was beaten to death and Xun was demoted to Prefect of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: when this was discovered Wei Bin was beaten to death and Huangfu Xun banished to prefect of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 業與妃惶懼待罪，上降階執業手曰：「吾若有心猜兄弟者，天地實殛之。」

translations.literal: Ye and his consort, fearful, awaited punishment; the emperor descended the steps, took Ye's hand, and said, "If I ever harbored suspicion against my brothers, may Heaven and Earth truly strike me dead."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ye and his consort waited in terror for punishment; the emperor came down the steps, took Ye's hand, and said, "If I ever meant to distrust my brothers, let Heaven and Earth strike me dead."

sentences.zh: 即與之宴飲，仍慰諭妃，令復位。

translations.literal: He immediately feasted and drank with him, and also comforted and instructed the consort, ordering her to resume her place.
translations.idiomatic: Then he feasted with Ye and reassured the princess, restoring her to her seat.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙卯，上還京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yimao, the emperor returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yimao, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 辛未，突厥寇甘、涼等州，敗河西節度使楊敬述，掠契苾部落而去。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Türks raided Gan, Liang, and other prefectures, defeated Hexi Military Commissioner Yang Jingshu, plundered the Qibi tribes, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the Türks raided Gan, Liang, and neighboring prefectures, routed Hexi commissioner Yang Jingshu, looted the Qibi tribes, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 先是，朔方大總管王晙奏請西發拔悉密，東方奚、契丹，期以今秋掩毘伽牙帳於稽落水上；

translations.literal: Previously, Shuofang Supreme Commander Wang Jun had submitted requesting to launch the Basmil in the west and the Xi and Khitan in the east, planning for that autumn to strike Bilge's royal camp at Jiluo Water;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shuofang supreme commander Wang Jun had proposed a joint autumn strike on Bilge's encampment at Jiluo Water—Basmil from the west, Xi and Khitan from the east—

sentences.zh: 毘伽聞之，大懼。

translations.literal: when Bilge heard of this, he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: when Bilge heard, he was terrified.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷曰：「不足畏也。

translations.literal: Tonyukuk said, "Not worth fearing.
translations.idiomatic: Tonyukuk said, "There is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 拔悉密在北庭，與奚、契丹相去絕遠，勢不相及；

translations.literal: The Basmil are at Beiting, extremely far from the Xi and Khitan—their forces cannot reach one another;
translations.idiomatic: The Basmil hold Beiting, far from the Xi and Khitan—they cannot coordinate;

sentences.zh: 朔方兵計亦不能來此。

translations.literal: the Shuofang troops by plan also cannot come here.
translations.idiomatic: and Shuofang's army cannot march this far in any case.

sentences.zh: 必若能來，俟其垂至，徙牙帳北行三日，唐兵食盡自去矣。

translations.literal: Even if they truly can come, wait until they are about to arrive, then move the royal camp north for three days' travel—the Tang troops will run out of food and leave of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If they do come, we need only move the royal camp three days north when they near—they will run out of supplies and leave.

sentences.zh: 且拔悉密輕而好利，得王晙之約，必喜而先至。

translations.literal: Moreover the Basmil are light-minded and greedy for profit; receiving Wang Jun's agreement, they will surely be delighted and arrive first.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Basmil are reckless and greedy; once Wang Jun's offer reaches them they will rush ahead eagerly.

sentences.zh: 晙與張嘉貞不相悅，奏請多不相應，必不敢出兵。

translations.literal: Jun and Zhang Jiazhen are not on good terms; their submitted requests often do not agree—he surely dares not send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Zhang Jiazhen despise each other—their plans never align, so Jun will never dare march.

sentences.zh: 晙兵不出，拔悉密獨至，擊而取之，勢甚易耳。」

translations.literal: If Jun's troops do not come out and the Basmil come alone, strike and take them—it would be very easy."
translations.idiomatic: With Jun staying home and the Basmil arriving alone, we can crush them with ease."

sentences.zh: 既而拔悉密果發兵逼突厥牙帳，而朔方及奚、契丹兵不至，拔悉密懼，引退。

translations.literal: Soon after, the Basmil indeed sent troops to press upon the Türk royal camp, but the Shuofang and Xi and Khitan troops did not arrive; the Basmil were afraid and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Basmil soon marched on the Türk royal camp, but Shuofang and the Xi and Khitan never came; frightened, the Basmil pulled back.

sentences.zh: 毘伽欲擊之，暾欲谷曰：「此屬去家千里，將死戰，未可擊也。

translations.literal: Bilge wished to strike them; Tonyukuk said, "These men are a thousand li from home and will fight to the death—it is not yet time to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Bilge wanted to attack, but Tonyukuk said, "They are a thousand li from home and will fight to the death—we should not engage them yet.

sentences.zh: 不如以兵躡之。」

translations.literal: Better to have troops follow after them."
translations.idiomatic: Better to follow at a distance."

sentences.zh: 去北庭二百里，暾欲谷分兵間道先圍北庭，因縱兵擊拔悉密，大破之。

translations.literal: Two hundred li from Beiting, Tonyukuk divided his troops, sent them by hidden routes first to surround Beiting, then unleashed his forces to strike the Basmil and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li from Beiting Tonyukuk split his force, sent a detachment by a hidden route to encircle Beiting, then fell on the Basmil and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 拔悉密眾潰走，趨北庭，不得入，盡為突厥所虜。

translations.literal: The Basmil host broke and fled, rushing toward Beiting; unable to enter, they were all captured by the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: The Basmil army fled toward Beiting but could not get in and were captured to the last man.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷引兵還，出赤亭，掠涼州羊馬，楊敬述遣裨將盧公利、判官元澄將兵邀擊之。

translations.literal: Tonyukuk led his troops back, emerged at Chiting, plundered sheep and horses of Liang Prefecture; Yang Jingshu dispatched Brigadier Lu Gongli and Administrative Aide Yuan Cheng to lead troops and intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Tonyukuk marched back through Chiting, looting sheep and horses in Liang Prefecture; Yang Jingshu sent brigadier Lu Gongli and aide Yuan Cheng to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷謂其眾曰：「吾乘勝而來，敬述出兵，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Tonyukuk said to his host, "I come riding victory; when Jingshu sends out troops, smashing them is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Tonyukuk told his men, "We come fresh from victory—when Jingshu sends troops we are sure to break them."

sentences.zh: 公利等至刪丹，與暾欲谷遇，唐兵大敗，公利，澄脫身走。

translations.literal: When Gongli and the others reached Shandan and encountered Tonyukuk, the Tang troops were utterly defeated; Gongli and Cheng escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: At Shandan Lu Gongli and Yuan Cheng met Tonyukuk; the Tang force was routed and the two commanders fled.

sentences.zh: 毘伽由是大振，盡有默啜之眾。

translations.literal: Bilge thereby greatly rose in power and wholly possessed Mochuo's host.
translations.idiomatic: Bilge's prestige soared, and he inherited all of Mochuo's following.

sentences.zh: 契丹牙官可突干驍勇得眾心，李娑固猜畏，欲去之。

translations.literal: Khitan military officer Ketugan was brave and fierce and won the people's hearts; Li Suogu was suspicious and fearful and wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan officer Ketugan was bold and beloved by the tribesmen; Li Suogu feared him and wanted him gone.

sentences.zh: 是歲，可突干舉兵擊娑固，娑固敗奔營州。

translations.literal: This year, Ketugan raised troops and attacked Suogu; Suogu was defeated and fled to Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year Ketugan rebelled, defeated Suogu, and drove him to flee to Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 營州都督許欽澹遣安東都護薛泰帥驍勇五百與奚王李大酺奉娑固以討之，戰敗，娑固、李大酺皆為可突干所殺，生擒薛泰，營州震恐。

translations.literal: Ying Prefecture Protector Xu Qindan dispatched Protector-General of Andong Xue Tai to lead five hundred picked warriors together with Xi King Li Da'pu to support Suogu in punishing [Ketugan]; they were defeated in battle; Suogu and Li Da'pu were both killed by Ketugan, Xue Tai was captured alive, and Ying Prefecture was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Protector Xu Qindan sent Andong protector-general Xue Tai with five hundred elite troops and Xi king Li Da'pu to restore Suogu; they were beaten—Suogu and Li Da'pu were killed, Xue Tai captured alive, and Ying Prefecture trembled.

sentences.zh: 許欽澹移軍入渝關，可突干立娑固從父弟郁干為主，遣使請罪。

translations.literal: Xu Qindan moved his army into Yuguan Pass; Ketugan installed Suogu's younger paternal cousin Yu'gan as ruler and dispatched envoys to request pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qindan withdrew his army into Yuguan Pass; Ketugan enthroned Suogu's cousin Yu'gan and sent envoys to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 上赦可突干之罪，以郁干為松漠都督，以李大酺之弟魯蘇為饒樂都督。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned Ketugan's crime and appointed Yügan Grand Protector of Songmo and Ludu, younger brother of Li Dafu, Grand Protector of Raole.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned Ketugan and made Yügan Grand Protector of Songmo and Li Dafu's younger brother Ludu Grand Protector of Raole.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，制削楊敬述官爵，以白衣檢校涼州都督，仍充諸使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, by edict Yang Jingshu's title and rank were stripped; he was appointed in plain dress as acting Governor of Liang Province and still retained his various envoy posts.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, an edict stripped Yang Jingshu of rank and title, appointed him acting Governor of Liang Province in plain dress, and kept him in his envoy assignments.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，改蒲州為河中府，置中都官僚，一准京兆、河南。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Pu Prefecture was changed to Hezhong Prefecture; a Middle Capital bureaucracy was established, all following the standard of Jingzhao and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the court changed Pu Prefecture to Hezhong Prefecture, installed a Middle Capital administration, and matched it to Jingzhao and Henan.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，上幸驪山溫湯；

translations.literal: On bingyin, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Emperor Xuanzong went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 乙亥，還宮。

translations.literal: On yihai, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 監察御史宇文融上言：「天下戶口逃移，巧偽甚眾，請加檢括。」

translations.literal: Censor Yuwen Rong submitted, saying, "Throughout the realm registered households have fled and relocated, and fraudulent evasion is extremely widespread—I ask that inspection and registration be intensified."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yuwen Rong memorialized: "Households are fleeing registration across the realm, and fraud is widespread—I ask that a thorough review be ordered."

sentences.zh: 融，弼之玄孫也，源乾曜素愛其才，贊成之。

translations.literal: Rong was the great-grandson of Bi; Yuan Qianyao had long admired his talent and supported him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong was the great-grandson of Yuwen Bi; Yuan Qianyao had long favored his abilities and backed the proposal.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙酉，敕有司議招集流移、按詰巧偽之法以聞。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yiyou, an edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate methods for gathering the displaced, investigating and punishing fraud, and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yiyou, the emperor ordered officials to draft methods for registering the displaced, exposing false claims, and reporting back.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，突厥毘伽復使來求和。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the Türk qaghan Bilge again sent envoys to request peace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Türk qaghan Bilge again sent envoys seeking peace.

sentences.zh: 上賜書，諭以「曩昔國家與突厥和親，華、夷安逸，甲兵休息；

translations.literal: The emperor sent a letter instructing him, "In times past when the state and the Türk were allied by marriage, Chinese and barbarian alike lived at ease and arms rested;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in reply: "When the state and the Türk were bound by marriage, China and the steppe alike lived in peace and armies stood down;

sentences.zh: 國家買突厥羊馬，突厥受國家繒帛，彼此豐給。

translations.literal: The state bought sheep and horses from the Türk, and the Türk received silks and cloth from the state—each side was abundantly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: The court bought Türk sheep and horses; the Türk received our silks and brocades—both sides prospered.

sentences.zh: 自數十年來，不復如舊，正由默啜無信，口和心叛，數出盜兵，寇抄邊鄙，人怨神怒，隕身喪元，吉凶之驗，皆可汗所見。

translations.literal: For several decades it has no longer been as before—precisely because Mojie was faithless, speaking peace while rebelling in heart, repeatedly sending raiding bands to plunder the borderlands; men resented and the gods were angered, and he perished and lost his head—the omens of fortune and calamity, as the qaghan himself has seen.
translations.idiomatic: For decades things have not been as they were—because Mojie broke faith, swore peace while plotting revolt, and sent raiders again and again against the frontier until heaven and men turned against him and he lost his life. The qaghan has seen with his own eyes how fortune and ruin are repaid.

sentences.zh: 今復蹈前跡，掩襲甘、涼，隨遣使人，更來求好。

translations.literal: Now you again follow the old track, launching surprise attacks on Gan and Liang, then sending envoys once more to seek friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Now you repeat the same course—striking Gan and Liang by surprise, then sending envoys to sue for peace again.

sentences.zh: 國家如天之覆，如海之容，但取來情，不追往咎。

translations.literal: The state is like heaven's canopy, like the sea's embrace—we look only to your present intent and do not pursue past faults.
translations.idiomatic: The state covers all as heaven covers and holds all as the sea holds—we heed your present sincerity and do not hunt old wrongs.

sentences.zh: 可汗果有誠心，則共保遐福；

translations.literal: If the qaghan truly has sincere intent, then together we shall preserve lasting blessing;
translations.idiomatic: If the qaghan is sincere, we may share lasting good fortune;

sentences.zh: 不然，無煩使者徒爾往來。

translations.literal: If not, there is no need for envoys to come and go in vain.
translations.idiomatic: If not, let your envoys stop wasting their journeys.

sentences.zh: 若其侵邊，亦有以待。

translations.literal: If you invade the border, we also have means awaiting you.
translations.idiomatic: If you raid the frontier again, we are ready for that as well.

sentences.zh: 可汗其審圖之！」

translations.literal: Qaghan, weigh this carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan, consider this carefully!"

sentences.zh: 丁亥，制：「州縣逃亡戶口聽百日自首，或於所在附籍，或牒歸故鄉，各從所欲。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict: "Fleeing households in prefectures and counties are allowed one hundred days to surrender themselves; they may register where they now live or return by certificate to their native place—each as he wishes.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai an edict declared: "Runaway households may turn themselves in within one hundred days, register where they are, or return home with a permit—as each prefers.

sentences.zh: 過期不首，即加檢括，謫徙邊州；

translations.literal: If after the deadline they do not surrender, registration will be enforced and they will be banished to border prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Those who fail to report in time will be hunted out and exiled to the frontier;

sentences.zh: 公私敢容庇者抵罪。」

translations.literal: Anyone public or private who dares to shelter them will be punished for the crime."
translations.idiomatic: anyone public or private who harbors them will be punished."

sentences.zh: 以宇文融充使，括逃移戶口及籍外田，所獲巧偽甚眾。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong was appointed commissioner to register fleeing households and fields outside the rolls; the fraud uncovered was extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong was made commissioner to track down displaced households and unregistered land; the fraud he found was vast.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部員外郎兼侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War and concurrently Serving Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of War and appointed serving censor as well.

sentences.zh: 融奏置勸農判官十人，並攝御史，分行天下。

translations.literal: Rong memorialized to establish ten agricultural promotion judges, each also acting as censor, sent throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Rong asked that ten agricultural promotion judges be named, each doubling as censor, and sent across the empire.

sentences.zh: 其新附客戶，免六年賦調。

translations.literal: Newly attached client households were exempt from taxes and corvée for six years.
translations.idiomatic: Newly registered client households were exempt from tax and corvée for six years.

sentences.zh: 使者競為刻急，州縣承風勞擾，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: The envoys vied in harshness; prefectures and counties followed the wind and weary harassment; the people suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioners competed to be harsh; local officials followed suit and harassed the people, who suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 陽翟尉皇甫憬上疏言其狀；

translations.literal: Huangfu Jing, magistrate of Yangzhai, submitted a memorial describing the situation;
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Jing, magistrate of Yangzhai, memorialized describing the abuse;

sentences.zh: 上方任融，貶憬盈川尉。

translations.literal: The emperor was then relying on Rong and demoted Jing to magistrate of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, still backing Rong, demoted Huangfu Jing to magistrate of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 州縣希旨，務於獲多，虛張其數，或以實戶為客，凡得戶八十餘萬，田亦稱是。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties curried favor, striving to seize more, inflating the numbers, sometimes listing actual households as clients; in all more than eight hundred thousand households were found, and fields in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials eager to please inflated their counts, sometimes listing real taxpayers as new clients; they claimed more than eight hundred thousand households and a matching amount of land.

sentences.zh: 蘭池州胡康待賓誘諸降戶同反，夏，四月，攻陷六胡州，有眾七萬，進逼夏州。

translations.literal: Kang Daibin, a Hu of Lanchi Prefecture, incited various surrendered households to rebel together; in summer, the fourth month, he captured Liuhu Prefecture, had a host of seventy thousand, and advanced to threaten Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Daibin, a non-Han of Lanchi Prefecture, urged surrendered tribes to rebel; in summer, in the fourth month, he took Liuhu Prefecture, raised seventy thousand men, and marched on Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 命朔方總管王晙、隴右節度使郭知運共討之。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, overall commander of Shuofang, and Guo Zhiyun, military governor of Longyou, were ordered jointly to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, commander of Shuofang, and Guo Zhiyun, military governor of Longyou, were ordered to suppress him together.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，敕：「京官五品以上，外官剌史、四府上佐，各舉縣令一人，視其政善惡，為舉者賞罰。」

translations.literal: On wuxu, an edict: "Capital officials of the fifth rank and above, and external officials—prefects and senior aides of the four superior prefectures—each shall recommend one county magistrate; according to the goodness or badness of his governance, the recommender shall be rewarded or punished."
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu an edict required capital officials of fifth rank and above and external prefects and senior aides of the four great prefectures each to recommend one county magistrate, with reward or punishment for the recommender according to the magistrate's performance."

sentences.zh: 以太僕卿王毛仲為朔方道防禦討擊大使，使與王晙及天兵軍節度大使張說相知討康待賓。

translations.literal: Grand Stable Master Wang Maochong was made Grand Ambassador for Defense and Punitive Attack on the Shuofang Circuit, to coordinate with Wang Jun and Zhang Yue, military governor of the Heavenly Troops Army, in suppressing Kang Daibin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Stable Master Wang Maochong was named grand ambassador for defense and punitive attack on the Shuofang circuit and told to join Wang Jun and Zhang Yue, military governor of the Heavenly Troops Army, against Kang Daibin.

sentences.zh: 六月，己卯，罷中都，復為蒲州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jimao, the Middle Capital was abolished and it reverted to Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jimao, the Middle Capital was abolished and the region restored to Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蒲州刺史陸象先政尚寬簡，吏民有罪，多曉諭遣之。

translations.literal: Lu Xiangxian, Prefect of Pu, in governance favored leniency and simplicity; when officials and people committed offenses he mostly admonished and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangxian, prefect of Pu, governed with leniency; when officials or commoners erred he usually warned them and let them go.

sentences.zh: 州錄事言於象先曰：「明公不施棰撻，何以示威！」

translations.literal: The prefectural recorder said to Xiangxian, "My lord, if you do not apply the rod and flogging, how will you display authority!"
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural clerk said to Lu Xiangxian, "My lord, without the rod how can you show authority!"

sentences.zh: 象先曰：「人情不遠，此屬豈不解吾言邪？

translations.literal: Xiangxian said, "Human feelings are not distant—will these people not understand my words?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangxian replied, "People are not far from understanding—surely they grasp what I mean?

sentences.zh: 必欲棰撻以示威，當從汝始！」

translations.literal: If you must have rod and flogging to display authority, then start with you!"
translations.idiomatic: If you want the rod to show authority, begin with yourself!"

sentences.zh: 錄事慚而退。

translations.literal: The recorder withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 像先嘗謂人曰：「天下本無事，但庸人擾之耳。

translations.literal: Xiangxian once said to others, "Under heaven there is originally nothing the matter—it is only mediocre men who stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangxian once said, "The realm is fundamentally at peace—it is meddlers who make trouble.

sentences.zh: 苟清其源，何憂不治！」

translations.literal: If only the source is cleared, why worry that it will not be well governed!"
translations.idiomatic: Clear the source and there is no fear of disorder!"

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己酉，王晙大破康待賓，生擒之，殺叛胡萬五千人。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiyou, Wang Jun greatly defeated Kang Daibin, captured him alive, and killed fifteen thousand rebel Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiyou, Wang Jun routed Kang Daibin, took him alive, and killed fifteen thousand rebel tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，集四夷酋長，腰斬康待賓於西市。

translations.literal: On xinyou, chieftains of the four barbarians were assembled, and Kang Daibin was cut in two at the waist in the Western Market.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou chieftains of the four peoples were gathered to watch Kang Daibin cut in two at the waist in the Western Market.

sentences.zh: 先是，叛胡潛與党項通謀，攻銀城、連谷，據其倉庾，張說將步騎萬人出合河關掩擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the rebel Hu had secretly conspired with the Tangut, attacked Yincheng and Liangu, and seized their granaries; Zhang Yue led ten thousand infantry and cavalry out through Hehe Pass in a surprise attack and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the rebels had secretly allied with the Tangut, struck Yincheng and Liangu, and seized the granaries; Zhang Yue led ten thousand foot and horse out through Hehe Pass and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 追至駱駝堰，党項乃更與胡戰，胡眾潰，西走入鐵建山。

translations.literal: Pursuit reached Luotuo Dam; the Tangut then turned to fight the Hu again; the Hu host collapsed and fled west into Mount Tiejian.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached Luotuo Dam; the Tangut then turned on the Hu again; the Hu broke and fled west into Mount Tiejian.

sentences.zh: 說安集党項，使復其居業。

translations.literal: Yue settled and gathered the Tangut and had them resume their dwellings and livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue resettled the Tangut and restored their homes and livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 討擊使阿史那獻以党項翻覆，請並誅之，說曰：「王者之師，當伐叛柔服，豈可殺已降邪！」

translations.literal: Punitive Commissioner Ashina Xian, because the Tangut had turned treacherous, asked that they all be executed together; Yue said, "The army of a true king should punish rebels and soothe those who submit—how can one kill those who have already surrendered!"
translations.idiomatic: Punitive commissioner Ashina Xian, citing Tangut treachery, asked to kill them all; Zhang Yue said, "A royal army punishes rebels and welcomes those who submit—how can we slaughter men who have yielded!"

sentences.zh: 因奏置麟州，以鎮撫党項餘眾。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized to establish Lin Prefecture to pacify and settle the remaining Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked that Lin Prefecture be established to watch over the remaining Tangut.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day yisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day yisi, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 康待賓之反也，詔郭知運與王晙相知討之；

translations.literal: When Kang Daibin rebelled, an edict ordered Guo Zhiyun and Wang Jun to coordinate in suppressing him;
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Daibin rebelled, the court ordered Guo Zhiyun and Wang Jun to cooperate against him;

sentences.zh: 晙上言，朔方兵自有餘力，請敕知運還本軍。

translations.literal: Jun submitted that the Shuofang army on its own had surplus strength and asked that Zhiyun be ordered to return to his original army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun reported that Shuofang troops alone were sufficient and asked that Guo Zhiyun be sent back to his command.

sentences.zh: 未報，知運已至，由是與晙不協。

translations.literal: Before a reply came, Zhiyun had already arrived; because of this he and Jun were not in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Before the court answered, Guo Zhiyun had already arrived; from then on he and Wang Jun failed to cooperate.

sentences.zh: 晙所招降者，知運復縱兵擊之；

translations.literal: Those whom Jun had summoned to surrender, Zhiyun again loosed troops to attack;
translations.idiomatic: Men Wang Jun had persuaded to surrender, Guo Zhiyun attacked again;

sentences.zh: 虜以晙為賣己，由是復叛。

translations.literal: The barbarians regarded Jun as having sold them out, and therefore rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes decided Wang Jun had betrayed them and rose again.

sentences.zh: 上以不能遂定群胡，丙午，貶晙為梓州刺史。
