translations.literal: Because he could not finally settle the various Hu, on bingwu the emperor demoted Jun to Prefect of Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Because the rebellion remained unsettled, on bingwu the emperor demoted Wang Jun to prefect of Zi.

sentences.zh: 丁未，梁文獻公姚崇薨，遺令：「佛以清淨慈悲為本，而愚者寫經造像，冀以求福。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Duke of Liang Wenzian Yao Chong died; his testamentary instruction: "The Buddha takes purity and compassion as foundation, yet fools copy sutras and make images, hoping thereby to seek blessing.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Duke of Liang Wenzian Yao Chong died, leaving instructions: "Buddhism rests on purity and compassion, yet fools copy sutras and cast images hoping for merit.

sentences.zh: 昔周、齊分據天下，周則毀經像而修甲兵，齊則崇塔廟而馳刑政，一朝合戰，齊滅周興。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou and Qi divided the realm; Zhou destroyed sutras and images and repaired armor and weapons, while Qi honored pagodas and temples and neglected punishments and government; in one morning they joined battle—Qi perished and Zhou rose.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou and Qi split the empire: Zhou tore down sutras and images and sharpened arms; Qi piled up temples and neglected justice—then they met in battle, and Qi fell while Zhou rose.

sentences.zh: 近者諸武、諸韋，造寺度人，不可勝紀，無救族誅。

translations.literal: Recently the Wus and the Weis built temples and ordained people beyond counting, yet it did not save them from the execution of their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago the Wu and Wei clans built temples and ordained monks without number, yet could not escape extermination.

sentences.zh: 汝曹勿效兒女子終身不寤，追薦冥福。

translations.literal: You must not imitate silly women and children who never wake in a lifetime, pursuing offerings for blessings in the dark realm.
translations.idiomatic: Do not imitate foolish men and women who never learn, piling up offerings for phantom blessings after death.

sentences.zh: 道士見僧獲利，效其所為，尤不可延之於家。

translations.literal: Daoist priests seeing monks profit imitated what they did—above all they must not be brought into the home.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoist priests saw monks prosper they copied them—above all, do not let such men into the house.

sentences.zh: 當永為後法！」

translations.literal: This shall forever be the law for posterity!"
translations.idiomatic: Let this be your rule forever!"

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以張說為兵部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On guihai, Zhang Yue was made Minister of War and Associate Grand Counselor of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Zhang Yue was made minister of war and associate grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，河西、隴右節度大使郭知運卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Guo Zhiyun, military governor of Hexi and Longyou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Guo Zhiyun, military governor of Hexi and Longyou, died.

sentences.zh: 知運與同縣右衛副率王君廓，皆以驍勇善騎射著名西陲，為虜所憚，時人謂之王、郭。

translations.literal: Zhiyun and Wang Junkuo of the same county, deputy commander of the Right Guard, were both famed on the western frontier for fierce valor and skill in horsemanship and archery; the barbarians feared them, and men of the time called them Wang and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhiyun and Wang Junkuo of the same county, deputy commander of the Right Guard, were famed on the western frontier for courage and archery; the tribes feared them, and people called them "Wang and Guo."

sentences.zh: 廓遂自知運麾下代為河西、隴右節度使，判涼州都督。

translations.literal: Junkuo then rose from under Zhiyun's command to replace him as military governor of Hexi and Longyou and concurrently Governor of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junkuo, who had served under Guo Zhiyun, succeeded him as military governor of Hexi and Longyou and acting governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙辰，國子祭酒元行衝上《群書四錄》，凡書四萬八千一百六十九卷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingchen, Grand Master of the National University Yuan Xingchong submitted the Comprehensive Catalogue of Books in Four Sections—in all forty-eight thousand one hundred sixty-nine scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingchen, Grand Master of the National University Yuan Xingchong presented the Comprehensive Catalogue of Books in Four Sections, listing 48,169 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 庚午，赦天下。

translations.literal: On gengwu, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙酉，上幸驪山溫湯；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiyou Emperor Xuanzong went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 壬辰，還宮。

translations.literal: On renchen, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，諸王為都督、刺史者，悉召還京師。

translations.literal: That year, all princes who served as overall commanders or prefects were summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year every prince serving as military commander or prefect was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 新作蒲津橋，熔鐵為牛以系絲亙。

translations.literal: A new bridge at Pujin was built; iron was melted to cast oxen to tie the cables spanning it.
translations.idiomatic: A new bridge was built at Pujin, with iron oxen cast to anchor the cables.

sentences.zh: 安州別駕劉子玄卒。

translations.literal: Liu Zixuan, Vice Prefect of Anzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zixuan, vice prefect of An Prefecture, died.

sentences.zh: 子玄即知幾也，避上嫌名，以字行。

translations.literal: Zixuan was Zhiji; to avoid the emperor's taboo name he went by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zixuan was Liu Zhiji; to avoid the emperor's taboo he used his style name.

sentences.zh: 著作郎吳兢撰《則天實錄》，言宋璟張說使證魏元忠事。

translations.literal: Archivist Wu Jing compiled the Veritable Record of Empress Zetian, stating that Song Jing and Zhang Yue were made to testify regarding Wei Yuanzhong's affair.
translations.idiomatic: Archivist Wu Jing compiled the Veritable Record of Empress Zetian, recording that Song Jing and Zhang Yue were compelled to testify in Wei Yuanzhong's case.

sentences.zh: 說修史見之，知兢所為，謬曰：「劉五殊不相借。」

translations.literal: Yue, while revising the history, saw it, knew it was Jing's work, and falsely said, "Liu the Fifth would never have lent this."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, editing the history, saw the passage, knew Wu Jing had written it, and falsely said, "Liu the Fifth would never have shared this with you."

sentences.zh: 兢起對曰：「此乃兢所為，史草具在，不可使明公枉怨死者。」

translations.literal: Jing rose and replied, "This was indeed done by Jing; the draft history is all here—we cannot let Your Excellency wrongly blame the dead."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing stood and answered, "I wrote this myself; the draft is here—Your Excellency must not wrongly blame the dead."

sentences.zh: 同僚皆失色。

translations.literal: All colleagues turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues blanched.

sentences.zh: 其後說陰祈兢改數字，兢終不許，曰：「若徇公請，則此史不為直筆，何以取信於後！」

translations.literal: Afterward Yue secretly besought Jing to change several characters; Jing ultimately would not agree, saying, "If I follow Your Excellency's request, then this history will not be straight writing—how can it win trust from posterity!"
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Yue privately asked Wu Jing to change a few words; Wu Jing refused, saying, "If I bow to Your Excellency, this history will no longer be honest—how can posterity trust it!"

sentences.zh: 太史上言，《麟德歷》浸疏，日食屢不效。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer submitted that the Linde Calendar grows increasingly inaccurate and solar eclipses repeatedly fail to prove correct.
translations.idiomatic: The grand astrologer reported that the Linde Calendar had grown unreliable and repeatedly failed to predict solar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 上命僧一行更造新歷，率府兵曹梁令瓚造黃道游儀以測候七政。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the monk Yixing to create a new calendar anew, and Liang Lingzan, military staff officer of the Stratagem Bureau, to build a ecliptic armillary sphere for observing the seven luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the monk Yixing to compile a new calendar and Liang Lingzan of the Stratagem Bureau to build a ecliptic armillary sphere to track the seven heavenly bodies.

sentences.zh: 置朔方節度使，領單于都護府，夏、鹽等六州，定遠、豐安二軍，三受降城。

translations.literal: A Shuofang military governor was established, overseeing the Chanyu Protectorate, the six prefectures including Xia and Yan, the two armies Dingyuan and Feng'an, and the three Accept-Surrender cities.
translations.idiomatic: A Shuofang military governor was installed over the Chanyu Protectorate, six prefectures including Xia and Yan, the Dingyuan and Feng'an armies, and the three Accept-Surrender fortresses.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁巳，上行幸東都，以刑部尚書王志愔為西京留守。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingsi, the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital; Wang Zhiyin, Minister of Justice, was made Western Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on dingsi Emperor Xuanzong went to the Eastern Capital and left Wang Zhiyin, minister of justice, as regent in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，命有司收公廨錢，以稅錢充百官俸。

translations.literal: On guihai, the relevant offices were ordered to collect official-hall funds and use tax money to cover officials' salaries.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the court ordered collection of official revenues and payment of salaries from tax receipts.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，收職田。

translations.literal: On yichou, official fields were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the court reclaimed official allotment lands.

sentences.zh: 畝率給倉粟二鬥。

translations.literal: Per mu, grain from storehouses was issued at the rate of two dou.
translations.idiomatic: Officials received two dou of granary grain per mu reclaimed.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊寅，上至東都。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuyin, the emperor reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuyin the emperor arrived at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己亥，以張說兼知朔方軍節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jihai, Zhang Yue was additionally made acting military governor of the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on jihai Zhang Yue was also named acting military governor of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 五月，伊、汝水溢，漂溺數千家。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Yi and Ru rivers overflowed and drowned several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Yi and Ru rivers flooded, drowning thousands of families.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬申，張說如朔方巡邊。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on renshen, Zhang Yue went to Shuofang to inspect the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on renshen Zhang Yue went to Shuofang to tour the frontier.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以餘姚縣主女慕容氏為燕郡公主，妻契丹王郁干。

translations.literal: On jichou, Murushi, daughter of the Princess of Yuyao County, was made Princess of Yan Commandery and given in marriage to the Khitan king Yügan.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Murushi, daughter of the Princess of Yuyao County, was made Princess of Yan Commandery and given to the Khitan king Yügan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁巳，博州河決，命按察使蕭嵩等治之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingsi, the Yellow River burst its banks in Bozhou; Investigating Commissioner Xiao Song and others were ordered to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingsi the Yellow River broke through at Bo Prefecture; investigating commissioner Xiao Song and others were ordered to control it.

sentences.zh: 嵩，梁明帝之孫之。

translations.literal: Song was grandson of Emperor Ming of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song was a grandson of Emperor Ming of Liang.

sentences.zh: 己巳，制增太廟為九室，遷中宗主還太廟。

translations.literal: On jisi, by edict the Imperial Ancestral Temple was expanded to nine chambers, and Emperor Zhongzong's tablet was moved back to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi an edict expanded the imperial ancestral temple to nine chambers and returned Emperor Zhongzong's spirit tablet to it.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，癸卯，武強令裴景仙，坐贓五千匹，事覺，亡命。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on guimao, Pei Jingxian, magistrate of Wuqiang, was guilty of five thousand bolts of embezzled goods; when the affair was discovered he fled as a fugitive.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, on guimao Pei Jingxian, magistrate of Wuqiang, was found to have embezzled five thousand bolts of silk and fled.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命集眾斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered him gathered before the crowd and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered him seized and executed before the public.

sentences.zh: 大理卿李朝隱奏景仙贓皆乞取，罪不至死。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Li Chaoyin submitted that Jingxian's embezzlement consisted entirely of solicited bribes, and that the crime did not merit death.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Li Chaoyin reported that Jingxian's graft had all been extorted by begging and did not warrant execution.

sentences.zh: 又，其曾祖寂有建義大功，載初中以非罪破家，惟景仙獨存，今為承嫡，宜宥其死，投之荒遠。

translations.literal: Further, his great-grandfather Ji had great merit in founding the dynasty; at the beginning of the Zaijue era the family was ruined for a faultless crime, and only Jingxian survived; now as heir of the main line, his death should be pardoned and he should be sent to remote wilds.
translations.idiomatic: He added that Jingxian's great-grandfather Ji had rendered great service at the founding; at the start of the Zaijue reign the clan was destroyed on a false charge, and Jingxian alone survived—now the heir of the main line, his life should be spared and he banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其辭略曰：「十代宥賢，功實宜錄；

translations.literal: His language in summary said, "Ten generations pardon the worthy, and merit truly ought to be recorded;
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran, in part: "Ten generations may spare the worthy, and true merit ought to be remembered;

sentences.zh: 一門絕祀，情或可哀。」

translations.literal: a single clan's line extinguished—emotionally perhaps pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: when a whole house faces extinction, pity is not out of place."

sentences.zh: 制令杖殺。

translations.literal: An edict ordered beating to death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 朝隱又奏曰：「生殺之柄，人主得專；

translations.literal: Chaoyin again submitted, saying, "The power of life and death the sovereign alone may wield;
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin submitted again: "The power of life and death belongs to the throne alone;

sentences.zh: 輕重有條，臣下當守。

translations.literal: lighter and heavier penalties have statutes, and subjects ought to uphold them.
translations.idiomatic: yet lighter and heavier punishments follow fixed statutes, and ministers must keep to them.

sentences.zh: 今若乞取得罪，便處斬刑；

translations.literal: Now if begging and taking is the crime, yet execution is imposed;
translations.idiomatic: If extortion alone is enough to draw the death penalty now,

sentences.zh: 後有枉法當科，欲加何辟？

translations.literal: when later there are perversions of law that merit punishment, what additional penalty would one add?
translations.idiomatic: what punishment remains for graver violations of law?

sentences.zh: 所以為國惜法，期守律文；

translations.literal: Therefore for the state's sake I cherish the law and hope to keep to the statutes;
translations.idiomatic: I plead for the law itself, hoping to preserve the statutes;

sentences.zh: 非敢以法隨人，曲矜仙命。」

translations.literal: I do not dare bend the law to follow a person and show partial favor to Xian's life."
translations.idiomatic: I do not mean to warp the law for a friend or show undue mercy to Jingxian."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「若寂勳都棄，仙罪特加，則叔向之賢，何足稱者；

translations.literal: He also said, "If Ji's merit is wholly cast aside and Xian's crime is specially increased, then what is Shu Xiang's worthiness worth praising;
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "If Ji's service is forgotten and Xian's penalty made heavier still, what becomes of Shu Xiang's celebrated wisdom—

sentences.zh: 若敖之鬼，不其餒而！」

translations.literal: would not the ghost of Ru'ao go hungry!"
translations.idiomatic: would not Ru'ao's shade starve for lack of offerings!"

sentences.zh: 上乃許之。

translations.literal: The emperor then granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong relented.

sentences.zh: 杖景仙一百，流嶺南惡處。

translations.literal: Jingxian was caned one hundred blows and exiled to an evil place in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian received a hundred strokes and was banished to the harshest reaches of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 安南賊帥梅叔焉等攻圍州縣，遣驃騎將軍兼內侍楊思勖討之。

translations.literal: The An'nan bandit chief Mei Shuyan and others attacked and besieged prefectures and counties; the emperor dispatched Chief Commandant of Cavalry and concurrently Palace Attendant Yang Sixun to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel chieftain Mei Shuyan of Annam and his allies besieged prefectures and counties, the court sent Chief Commandant of Cavalry and palace attendant Yang Sixun against them.

sentences.zh: 思勖募群蠻子弟，得兵十餘萬，襲擊，大破之，斬叔焉，積屍為京觀而還。

translations.literal: Sixun recruited sons and younger brothers from the various Miao tribes, obtained more than a hundred thousand troops, made a surprise attack, and greatly defeated them; he beheaded Shuyan, piled the corpses into a victory mound, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun raised more than a hundred thousand tribal auxiliaries, struck by surprise, and routed the rebels; he executed Shuyan, stacked the dead into a victory mound, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 初，上之誅韋氏也，王皇后頗預密謀，及即位數年，色衰愛弛。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor executed the Wei clan, Empress Wang had taken part in the secret plot; after several years on the throne, her beauty faded and his affection waned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong had overthrown Empress Wei's faction, Empress Wang had helped in the plot; but after several years on the throne her beauty faded and his favor cooled.

sentences.zh: 武惠妃有寵，陰懷傾奪之志。

translations.literal: Consort Wu the Graceful had favor and secretly harbored the ambition to overturn and seize [the position].
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu the Graceful held his affection and secretly plotted to supplant her.

sentences.zh: 後心不平，時對上有不遜語。

translations.literal: The empress was dissatisfied at heart and at times spoke irreverently to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress nursed her grievance and sometimes spoke sharply to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上愈不悅，密與秘書監姜皎謀以後無子廢之，皎洩其言。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still less pleased and secretly with Palace Library Director Jiang Jiao plotted to depose her because she had no son; Jiao leaked the words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong's displeasure deepened; he secretly conspired with Palace Library Director Jiang Jiao to depose her for bearing no son, and Jiao let the plan slip.

sentences.zh: 嗣滕王嶠，後之妹夫也，奏之。

translations.literal: Succession Prince of Teng Qiao, the empress's brother-in-law, reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao, Prince of Teng and the empress's brother-in-law, reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上怒，張嘉貞希旨構成其罪，云：「皎妄談休咎。」

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged; Zhang Jiazhen, seeking to please him, constructed his guilt, saying, "Jiao recklessly discussed fortune and misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was furious; Zhang Jiazhen, eager to please, framed the charge: "Jiao spoke recklessly of omens and fate."

sentences.zh: 甲戌，杖皎六十，流欽州，弟吏部侍郎晦貶春州司馬；

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Jiao was caned sixty blows and exiled to Qin Prefecture; his younger brother Vice Minister of Personnel Hui was demoted to aide of Chun Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Jiang Jiao received sixty strokes and was exiled to Qinzhou; his brother Hui, Vice Minister of Personnel, was demoted to military aide in Chunzhou;

sentences.zh: 親黨坐流、死者數人，皎卒於道。

translations.literal: Relatives and associates implicated—several were exiled or died; Jiao died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Several kinsmen and associates were exiled or executed, and Jiao died on the road.

sentences.zh: 己亥，敕：「宗室、外戚、駙馬，非至親毋得往還；

translations.literal: On jihai, an edict: "Imperial clansmen, maternal relatives, and imperial sons-in-law—unless the closest kin, must not come and go freely;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai an edict declared: "Members of the imperial clan, maternal kin, and imperial sons-in-law may not visit one another unless they are closest relatives;

sentences.zh: 其卜相占候之人，皆不得出入百官之家。」

translations.literal: Those who practice divination, physiognomy, and prognostication—all must not enter or leave the households of the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: diviners, physiognomers, and astrologers are forbidden to enter officials' houses."

sentences.zh: 己卯夜，左領軍兵曹權楚璧與其黨李齊損等作亂，立楚璧兄子梁山為光帝，詐稱襄王之子，擁左屯營兵數百人入宮城，求留守王志愔，不獲。

translations.literal: On the night of jimao, Left Army Adjutant Quan Chubi and his faction Li Qisun and others made rebellion; they enthroned Chubi's elder brother's son Liangshan as Emperor Guang, falsely claiming him as the son of the Prince of Xiang, and with several hundred soldiers of the Left Garrison Camp entered the palace city, seeking Regent Wang Zhiyin—they did not find him.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of jimao, Left Army adjutant Quan Chubi and his accomplice Li Qisun rebelled, enthroning Chubi's nephew Liangshan as Emperor Guang and claiming he was the Prince of Xiang's son; with several hundred men of the Left Garrison they entered the palace city seeking Regent Wang Zhiyin, but could not find him.

sentences.zh: 比曉，屯營兵自潰；

translations.literal: By dawn, the garrison troops dispersed on their own;
translations.idiomatic: By daybreak the camp soldiers had scattered;

sentences.zh: 斬楚璧等，傳首東都。

translations.literal: Chubi and others were beheaded, and their heads were sent to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chubi and his companions were executed and their heads sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 志愔驚怖而薨。

translations.literal: Zhiyin died of fright and terror.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiyin died of shock and terror.

sentences.zh: 楚璧，懷恩之侄；

translations.literal: Chubi was Huai'en's nephew;
translations.idiomatic: Chubi was a nephew of Huai'en;

sentences.zh: 齊損，迥秀之子也。

translations.literal: Qisun was Jiongxiu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Qisun was the son of Jiongxiu.

sentences.zh: 壬午，遣河南尹王怡如京師，按問宣慰。

translations.literal: On renwu, Henan Intendant Wang Yi was dispatched to the capital to investigate and offer consolation.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the court sent Henan Intendant Wang Yi to the capital to investigate and reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 癸未，吐蕃圍小勃律王沒謹忙，謹忙求救於北庭節度使張嵩曰：「勃律，唐之西門，勃律亡則西域皆為吐蕃矣。」

translations.literal: On guiwei, Tibet besieged the king of Lesser Bolü, Mojinmang; Mojinmang begged aid from Beiting Military Commissioner Zhang Song, saying, "Bolü is Tang's western gate; if Bolü perishes, then all the Western Regions will belong to Tibet."
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the Tibetans besieged Mojinmang, king of Lesser Bolü; he appealed to Beiting military commissioner Zhang Song: "Bolü is Tang's western gate—if Bolü falls, the whole Western Regions will pass to Tibet."

sentences.zh: 嵩乃遣疏勒副使張思禮將蕃、漢步騎四千人救之，晝夜倍道，與謹忙合擊吐蕃，大破之，斬獲數萬。

translations.literal: Song then dispatched Shule deputy envoy Zhang Silü at the head of four thousand Tibetan and Han infantry and cavalry to rescue them; day and night they doubled their pace, joined with Mojinmang in a combined attack on Tibet, and greatly defeated them, beheading and capturing tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Song sent Shule deputy commissioner Zhang Silü with four thousand mixed Tibetan and Han infantry and cavalry; marching day and night at forced pace, they joined Mojinmang, routed the Tibetans, and took tens of thousands of heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 自是累歲吐蕃不敢犯邊。

translations.literal: From this, for many years Tibet did not dare offend the border.
translations.idiomatic: For years afterward the Tibetans did not dare raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 王怡漢權楚璧獄，連逮甚眾，久之不決；

translations.literal: Wang Yi tried the Quan Chubi case; many were implicated in succession, and for a long time no decision was reached;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi's prosecution of the Quan Chubi affair dragged on, implicating a great many people;

sentences.zh: 上乃以開府儀同三司宋璟為西京留守。

translations.literal: The emperor then made Song Jing, Grand Master with Gold Seal and Pomp of the Three Excellencies, Western Capital Regent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong then named Song Jing, Grand Master of the Court with Imperial Pomp, regent of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 璟至，止誅同謀數人，餘皆奏原之。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived, he executed only several co-conspirators and memorialized that the rest be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing executed only a handful of ringleaders and petitioned to pardon the rest.

sentences.zh: 康待賓餘黨康願子反，自稱可汗；

translations.literal: Kang Daibin's remaining follower Kang Yuanzi rebelled and proclaimed himself qaghan;
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yuanzi, a holdout of Kang Daibin's faction, rebelled and styled himself qaghan;

sentences.zh: 張說發兵追討擒之，其黨悉平。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue dispatched troops in pursuit, captured him, and all his followers were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue sent troops in pursuit, captured him, and wiped out the remnants.

sentences.zh: 徙河曲六州殘胡五萬餘口於許、汝、唐、鄧、仙、豫等州，空河南、朔方千里之地。

translations.literal: More than fifty thousand surviving Hu of the six prefectures of the River Bend were moved to Xu, Ru, Tang, Deng, Xian, Yu, and other prefectures, emptying a thousand li of land in Henan and Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty thousand surviving nomads from the six River Bend prefectures were resettled in Xu, Ru, Tang, Deng, Xian, Yu, and elsewhere, leaving a thousand li of Henan and Shuofang depopulated.

sentences.zh: 先是，緣邊戍兵常六十餘萬，說以時無強寇，奏罷二十餘萬使還農。

translations.literal: Earlier, frontier garrison troops regularly numbered more than six hundred thousand; Yue, considering that at the time there were no strong enemies, submitted to dismiss more than two hundred thousand and send them back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrisons had long held more than six hundred thousand men; Zhang Yue argued that with no strong foe at hand, two hundred thousand could be sent home to farm.

sentences.zh: 上以為疑，說曰：「臣久在疆場，具知其情，將帥苟以自衛及役使營私而已。

translations.literal: The emperor was doubtful; Yue said, "Your subject has long been on the frontier and fully knows the situation—the generals only use them for self-protection and for corvée service to pursue private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was uneasy; Zhang Yue said, "I have served long on the frontier and know the truth: commanders keep these men only to guard themselves and to press them into private service.

sentences.zh: 若禦敵制勝，不必多相冗卒以妨農務。

translations.literal: If one wishes to resist the enemy and secure victory, one need not many redundant soldiers to hamper agricultural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: To fight and win, masses of idle troops are not needed—and they only harm the harvest.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以為疑，臣請以闔門百口保之。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty is doubtful, your subject requests to guarantee this with the hundred mouths of his entire household."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty still doubts me, I pledge my whole household—every soul under my roof."

sentences.zh: 上乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor then followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，諸衛府兵，自成丁從軍，六十而免，其家又不免雜徭，浸以貧弱，逃亡略盡，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the guard garrison troops of the various guards, from coming of age served in the army, at sixty were released; their households were still not exempt from miscellaneous corvée; gradually they grew poor and weak, and desertions were nearly complete—the common people suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: Guardsmen had once entered service at adulthood and mustered out at sixty, yet their families still owed corvée; poverty deepened, desertions emptied the ranks, and the people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 張說建議，請召募壯士充宿衛，不問色役，優為之制，逋逃者必爭出應募；

translations.literal: Zhang Yue proposed requesting to recruit strong men to fill the palace guard, not asking about corvée categories, granting them favorable terms—with deserters sure to compete to come forward and enlist;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue proposed recruiting stout men for palace guard duty, waiving corvée obligations and offering favorable terms—so fugitives would rush to enlist;

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong approved.

sentences.zh: 旬日，得精兵十三萬，分隸諸衛，更番上下。

translations.literal: Within ten days, one hundred thirty thousand elite troops were obtained, distributed among the various guards, rotating up and down in turns.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he raised a hundred thirty thousand trained men, assigned them to the guard corps, and organized them in rotating shifts.

sentences.zh: 兵農之分，從此始矣。

translations.literal: The division between soldier and farmer began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: From this began the formal split between soldier and farmer.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸丑，復以乾元殿為明堂。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guichou, Qianyuan Hall was again made the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the tenth month's guichou day, Qianyuan Hall was restored as the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上幸壽安興泰宮，獵於上宜川；

translations.literal: On jiayin, the emperor visited Shou'an Xingtai Palace and hunted at Shangyi Stream;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Emperor Xuanzong visited Shou'an Xingtai Palace and hunted along the Shangyi River;

sentences.zh: 庚申，還宮。

translations.literal: On gengshen, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 上欲耀兵北邊，丁卯，以秦州都督張守潔等為諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to display troops on the northern frontier; on dingmao, Qin Prefecture commander Zhang Shoujie and others were made generals of the various guards.
translations.idiomatic: Intent on showing force along the northern border, on dingmao he made Qinzhou commander Zhang Shoujie and others generals of the guard corps.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙未，初令宰相共食實封三百戶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yiwei, for the first time chancellors were jointly granted actual enfeoffment of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yiwei, chancellors were for the first time granted shared revenue fiefs of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 前廣州都督裴胄先下獄，上與宰相議其罪。

translations.literal: Former Guangzhou commander Pei Zouxian was imprisoned; the emperor discussed his crime with the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Former Guangzhou commander Pei Zouxian was in prison, and Emperor Xuanzong consulted the chancellors on his sentence.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞請杖之，張說曰：「臣聞刑不上大夫，為其近於君，且所以養廉恥也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen requested that he be caned; Zhang Yue said, "Your subject has heard that punishment does not reach grandees, because they are close to the sovereign, and also because it nurtures integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen urged a beating; Zhang Yue objected: "I have heard that punishment does not touch grand officers—they stand near the throne, and the law preserves their honor.

sentences.zh: 故士可殺不可辱。

translations.literal: Therefore a gentleman may be killed but may not be humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman may be executed, but not disgraced.

sentences.zh: 臣向巡北邊，聞杖姜皎於朝堂。

translations.literal: Your subject recently toured the northern frontier and heard that Jiang Jiao was caned in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: When I toured the north I learned that Jiang Jiao was beaten in open court.

sentences.zh: 皎官登三品，亦有微功，有罪應死則死，應流則流，奈何輕加笞辱，以皁隸待之！

translations.literal: Jiao's rank reached the third grade and he also had slight merit; if guilty he should die then die, if he should be exiled then be exiled—why lightly add beating and humiliation, treating him like a black-clad menial!
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jiao held third rank and had done some service—if guilty he should die or be exiled as the law requires; why belittle him with a beating, as if he were a menial servant!

sentences.zh: 姜皎事往，不可復追，胄先據狀當流，豈可復蹈前失！」

translations.literal: Jiang Jiao's affair is past and cannot be pursued again; Zouxian according to the facts ought to be exiled—how can we again repeat the former error!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jiao's case is past amending; Zouxian's crime calls for exile on the record—must we repeat that mistake?"

sentences.zh: 上深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞不悅，退謂說曰：「何論事之深也！」

translations.literal: Jiazhen was displeased; on retiring he said to Yue, "Why discuss the matter so deeply!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen was displeased; as they withdrew he said to Zhang Yue, "Why argue the point so hard!"

sentences.zh: 說曰：「宰相，時來則為之。

translations.literal: Yue said, "Chancellor—when the time comes one holds the post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue replied, "Chancellor is an office one holds only for a season.

sentences.zh: 若國之大臣皆可笞辱，但恐行及吾輩。

translations.literal: If all the state's great ministers may be beaten and humiliated, I only fear it will reach us as well.
translations.idiomatic: If any great minister may be beaten, the practice may reach us next.

sentences.zh: 吾此言非為胄先，乃為天下士君子也。」

translations.literal: My words here are not for Zouxian's sake but for the gentlemen of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: I speak not for Zouxian alone, but for every gentleman in the empire."

sentences.zh: 嘉貞無以應。

translations.literal: Jiazhen had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen had no answer.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子，以十姓可汗阿史那懷道女為交河公主，嫁突騎施可汗蘇祿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, the daughter of the Ten Surnames Qaghan Ashina Huaidao was made Princess Jiaohe and married to Turgesh Qaghan Suluo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, the daughter of the Ten Surnames qaghan Ashina Huaidao was created Princess Jiaohe and given in marriage to Suluo, qaghan of the Turgesh.

sentences.zh: 上將幸晉陽，因還長安。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to visit Jinyang and then return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong planned to visit Jinyang and then return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 張說言於上曰：「汾陰睢上有漢家后土祠，其禮久廢；

translations.literal: Zhang Yue spoke to the emperor, saying, "At Fenyin on Mount Sui is the Han dynasty shrine to the Empress of Earth; its rites have long been abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue said to the emperor: "At Fenyin, on Mount Sui, stands the Han shrine to the Empress of Earth, long neglected;

sentences.zh: 陛下宜因巡幸修之，為農祈谷。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to take advantage of the tour to restore it and pray for grain on behalf of agriculture."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should restore it during this tour and pray for the harvest."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 上女永穆公主將下嫁，敕資送如太平公主故事。

translations.literal: The emperor's daughter Princess Yongmu was about to marry; an edict ordered that her dowry match the precedent of Princess Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong's daughter Princess Yongmu was to marry; he ordered her dowry to match Princess Taiping's.

sentences.zh: 僧一行諫曰：「武後惟太平一女，故資送特厚，卒以驕敗，奈何為法！」

translations.literal: The monk Yixing remonstrated, saying, "Empress Wu had only Taiping as a daughter, so the dowry was especially generous—and in the end pride brought ruin; how can this become precedent!"
translations.idiomatic: The monk Yixing objected: "Empress Wu had only one daughter, Taiping—hence the lavish gift, which fed her pride and ruin. Why make that the standard!"

sentences.zh: 上遽止之。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately stopped this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong halted the order at once.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己巳，車駕自東都北巡；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jisi, the imperial carriage set out from the Eastern Capital on a northern tour;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's jisi day, the court left Luoyang on a northern progress;

sentences.zh: 庚辰，至潞州，給復五年；

translations.literal: On gengchen, it reached Luzhou and granted five years of tax remission;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen they reached Luzhou and remitted taxes for five years;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，至并州，置北都，以并州為太原府，刺史為尹；

translations.literal: On xinmao, it reached Bingzhou, established the Northern Capital, made Bingzhou Taiyuan Prefecture, and the prefect became intendant;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao they reached Bingzhou, established the Northern Capital, renamed Bingzhou Taiyuan Prefecture, and styled its prefect intendant;

sentences.zh: 二月，戊申，還至晉州。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wushen, it returned and reached Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wushen, they returned as far as Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 張說與張嘉貞不平，會嘉貞弟金吾將軍嘉祐贓發，說勸嘉貞素服待罪於外。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue and Zhang Jiazhen were on bad terms; it happened that Jiazhen's younger brother Gold Crow general Jiayou's embezzlement was exposed; Yue advised Jiazhen to wear plain clothes and await punishment outside.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue and Zhang Jiazhen were at odds; when Jiazhen's brother Jiayou, a Gold Crow general, was caught in graft, Yue urged Jiazhen to wait outside the palace in mourning dress to accept blame.

sentences.zh: 己酉，左遷嘉貞幽州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Jiazhen was demoted to prefect of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Jiazhen was demoted to prefect of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬子，祭后土於汾陰。

translations.literal: On renzi, the Empress of Earth was sacrificed to at Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the emperor sacrificed to the Empress of Earth at Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，貶平遙令王同慶為贛尉，坐廣為儲偫，煩擾百姓也。

translations.literal: On yimao, Pingyao magistrate Wang Tongqing was demoted to aide of Gan, on account of broadly storing supplies and troubling the common people.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Pingyao magistrate Wang Tongqing was demoted to deputy in Ganzhou for stockpiling supplies on a vast scale and harassing the people.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以張說兼中書令。

translations.literal: On guihai, Zhang Yue was made concurrently Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Zhang Yue was appointed concurrently Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 己巳，罷天兵、大武等軍，以大同軍為太原以北節度使，領太原、遼、石、嵐、汾、代、忻、朔、蔚、雲十州。

translations.literal: On jisi, the Heavenly Troops, Great Martial, and other armies were abolished; the Datong Army was made military commissioner north of Taiyuan, overseeing Taiyuan, Liao, Shi, Lan, Fen, Dai, Xin, Shuo, Yu, and Yun—ten prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the Heavenly Troops, Great Martial, and other armies were disbanded; the Datong Army was made military commissioner for the region north of Taiyuan, overseeing ten prefectures: Taiyuan, Liao, Shi, Lan, Fen, Dai, Xin, Shuo, Yu, and Yun.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚午，車駕至京師。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengwu, the imperial carriage reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengwu, the court reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子，以吏部尚書王晙為兵部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiazi, Minister of Personnel Wang Jun was made Minister of War and Associate Counselor with the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fourth month's jiazi day, Minister of Personnel Wang Jun was made Minister of War and associate counselor.

sentences.zh: 五月，己丑，以王晙兼朔方軍節度大使，巡河西、隴右、河東、河北諸軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jichou, Wang Jun was made concurrently Grand Ambassador of the Shuofang Army and toured the armies of Hexi, Longyou, Hedong, and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jichou, Wang Jun was named concurrently grand ambassador of the Shuofang Army and sent to inspect the forces of Hexi, Longyou, Hedong, and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 上置麗正書院，聚文學之士。

translations.literal: The emperor established the Lizheng Academy and gathered men of letters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong founded the Lizheng Academy and gathered literary scholars.

sentences.zh: 秘書監徐堅、太常博士會稽賀知章、監察御史鼓城趙冬曦等，或修書，或侍講，以張說為修書使以總之，有司供給優厚。

translations.literal: Palace Library Director Xu Jian, Regular Affairs Academic of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Kuaiji He Zhizhang, Investigating Censor Gucheng Zhao Dongxi, and others—some compiled books, some lectured; Zhang Yue was made compilation commissioner to oversee them, and the relevant offices supplied them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Library Director Xu Jian, Court of Imperial Sacrifices academic He Zhizhang of Kuaiji, investigating censor Zhao Dongxi of Gucheng, and others—some edited texts, some lectured—with Zhang Yue as chief compiler; the ministries supported them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人洛陽陸堅以為此屬無益於國，徒為糜費，欲悉奏罷之。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Luoyang Lu Jian considered that this group was of no benefit to the state and was merely wasteful spending; he wished to memorialize abolishing all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Lu Jian of Luoyang argued the academy served no state purpose and only wasted funds; he sought to petition for its abolition.

sentences.zh: 張說曰：「自古帝王於國家無事之時，莫不崇宮室，廣聲色。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue said, "Since antiquity emperors and kings, when the state had nothing to do, all exalted palaces and broadened music and women.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue replied: "Emperors in untroubled times have always raised palaces and filled them with music and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 今天子獨延禮文儒，發揮典籍，所益者大，所損者微。

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven alone extends courtesy to literary scholars and brings forth the classics—what is gained is great, what is lost is slight.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor alone honors scholars and revives the classics—the gain is great, the cost slight.

sentences.zh: 陸子之言，何不達也！」

translations.literal: Master Lu's words—how lacking in understanding!"
translations.idiomatic: Master Lu's objections show little sense of proportion!"

sentences.zh: 上聞之，重說而薄堅。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he valued Yue and looked lightly on Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong heard this, he held Zhang Yue in higher regard and thought less of Lu Jian.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，癸卯，敕：「前令檢括逃人，慮成煩擾。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on guimao, an edict: "The earlier order to round up fugitives—I fear it will become troublesome.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the eighth month's guimao day, an edict declared: "The recent order to hunt down fugitives risks becoming a source of abuse.

sentences.zh: 天下大同，宜各從所樂，令所在州縣安集，遂其生業。」

translations.literal: Under heaven there is great harmony—it is fitting that each follow what delights him; order the prefectures and counties where they are to settle them in peace and let them pursue their livelihoods."
translations.idiomatic: Under heaven all is at peace; let each man follow his own desire, and order every prefecture and county to receive and settle them, that they may pursue their livelihoods."

sentences.zh: 戊申，尊宣皇帝廟號獻祖，光皇帝廟號懿祖，祔於太廟九室。

translations.literal: On wushen, Emperor Xuan was honored with temple name Xianzu, Emperor Guang with temple name Yizu, and both were enshrined in the nine chambers of the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the court gave Emperor Xuan the temple name Xianzu and Emperor Guang the name Yizu, and installed both in the nine chambers of the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐谷渾畏吐蕃之強，附之者數年，九月，壬申，帥眾詣沙州降，河西節度使張敬忠撫納之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Tuyuhun, fearing Tibet's strength, had been attached to them for several years; in the ninth month, on renshen, they led their host to Shazhou to surrender, and Hexi military commissioner Zhang Jingzhong received and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun, fearing Tibetan power, had been under Tibetan sway for years; in the ninth month, on renshen, they brought their people to Shazhou to surrender, and Hexi commissioner Zhang Jingzhong received them.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，上幸驪山，作溫泉宮；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou, the emperor visited Mount Li and built the Hot Spring Palace;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the tenth month's dingyou day, Emperor Xuanzong went to Mount Li and built the Hot Spring Palace;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，還宮。

translations.literal: On jiayin, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，禮儀使張說等奏，以高祖配昊天上帝，罷三祖並配之禮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Rites Commissioner Zhang Yue and others memorialized that Emperor Gaozu should be paired with the Supreme Heavenly God, abolishing the rite of jointly pairing the three ancestral emperors.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Zhang Yue, commissioner of rites, and others proposed pairing Emperor Gaozu with the Supreme Heavenly God and ending the rite that had paired all three founding ancestors.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上祀南郊，赦天下。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and granted a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Emperor Xuanzong sacrificed at the Southern Altar and granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 戊子，命尚書左丞蕭嵩與京兆、蒲、同、岐、華州長官選府兵及白丁一十二萬，謂之「長從宿衛」，一年兩番，州縣毋得雜役使。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Xiao Song was ordered, together with the chief officials of Jingzhao, Pu, Tong, Qi, and Hua prefectures, to select one hundred twenty thousand garrison troops and common conscripts, calling them "long-service palace guards"—two rotations a year—with prefectures and counties forbidden to employ them for miscellaneous corvée.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the court ordered Vice Director Xiao Song and the chief officials of Jingzhao, Pu, Tong, Qi, and Hua to enlist 120,000 garrison troops and conscripts as "long-service palace guards," on two rotations a year, with prefectures and counties forbidden to use them for other corvée duties.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲午，上幸鳳泉湯；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, the emperor visited the Fengquan Hot Springs;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, Emperor Xuanzong went to the Fengquan hot springs;

sentences.zh: 戊申，還宮。

translations.literal: On wushen, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚申，兵部尚書、同中書門下三品王晙坐黨引疏族，貶蘄州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Minister of War and Associate Counselor Wang Jun, on account of factionalism involving distantly related clansmen, was demoted to prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Minister of War and associate counselor Wang Jun was demoted to prefect of Qizhou for factional ties with distant kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 是歲，張說奏改政事堂曰中書門下，列五房於其後，分掌庶政。

translations.literal: That year, Zhang Yue memorialized to change the Hall of Administration Affairs to "Central Secretariat and Chancellery," establishing five bureaus behind it to share administration of general affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Yue proposed renaming the Hall of Administration Affairs the Chancellery Secretariat, with five bureaus behind it to divide routine business.

sentences.zh: 初，監察御史濮陽杜暹因按事至突騎施，突騎施饋之金，暹固辭。

translations.literal: Initially, Investigating Censor Puyang Du Xian, while on an investigative tour, reached the Turgesh; the Turgesh presented him with gold, and Xian firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, investigating censor Du Xian of Puyang, on circuit duty, reached the Turgesh, who offered him gold; he refused.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「君寄身異域，不宜逆其情。」

translations.literal: Those at his side said, "Sir, you have entrusted yourself to a foreign land—it is not fitting to go against their wishes."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "You are a guest in a foreign land—you should not refuse their goodwill."

sentences.zh: 乃受之，埋於幕下，出境，移牒令取之。

translations.literal: So he accepted it, buried it beneath his tent, and upon leaving the border sent a dispatch ordering them to retrieve it.
translations.idiomatic: So he accepted it, buried it under his tent, and after crossing the border sent a note telling them to come fetch it.

sentences.zh: 虜大驚，度磧追之，不及。

translations.literal: The barbarians were greatly alarmed; they crossed the desert in pursuit but could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: The Turgesh were astonished; they crossed the desert in pursuit but could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 及安西都護闕，或薦暹往使安西，人服其清慎。

translations.literal: When the post of Protector-General of Anxi fell vacant, some recommended Xian to go and serve in Anxi; men admired his integrity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of protector-general of Anxi fell vacant, some recommended Du Xian; all respected his integrity and discretion.

sentences.zh: 時暹自給事中居母憂。

translations.literal: At that time Xian was in mourning for his mother, having resigned his post as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xian was then in mourning for his mother, having left his post as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，甲子，起暹為安西副大都護、磧西節度等使。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, on jiazi, Xian was recalled and made Deputy Protector-General of Anxi and military commissioner of Qixi and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the third month's jiazi day, Du Xian was recalled from mourning and made deputy protector-general of Anxi and commissioner of Qixi.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追復澤王上金官爵，求得庶子義珣於嶺南，紹其故封。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, Prince Ze Shangjin's titles and rank were posthumously restored; his illegitimate son Yixun was found in Lingnan and succeeded to his former fief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era Prince Ze Shangjin's rank was posthumously restored; his illegitimate son Yixun was found in Lingnan and given his old title.

sentences.zh: 許王素節之子瓘，利其爵邑，與弟璆謀，使人告義珣非上金子，妄冒襲封，復流嶺南，以璆繼上金後為嗣澤王。

translations.literal: Prince Xu's son Sujie, Suo, coveting the title and fief, conspired with his younger brother Qiu and had men report that Yixun was not Shangjin's son and had falsely usurped the succession; Yixun was again exiled to Lingnan, and Qiu succeeded Shangjin as heir Prince of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Suo, son of Prince Xu Sujie, coveted the fief and with his brother Qiu had men accuse Yixun of falsely claiming descent from Shangjin; Yixun was exiled again to Lingnan and Qiu was made heir Prince of Ze.

sentences.zh: 至是，玉真公主表義珣實上金子，為瓘兄弟所擯。

translations.literal: At this point, Princess Yuzhen memorialized that Yixun was indeed Shangjin's son and had been ousted by Suo and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Now Princess Yuzhen memorialized that Yixun was truly Shangjin's son and had been driven out by Suo and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子，復立義珣為嗣澤王，削璆爵，貶瓘鄂州別駕。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengzi, Yixun was again established as heir Prince of Ze; Qiu's rank was stripped and Suo was demoted to vice-prefect of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fourth month's gengzi day, Yixun was restored as heir Prince of Ze; Qiu was stripped of rank and Suo demoted to vice-prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，敕宗室旁繼為嗣王者並令歸宗。

translations.literal: On renyin, an edict ordered that all princes of the imperial clan who had been adopted as heirs from collateral lines should return to their original clans.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin an edict required collateral heirs among the imperial princes to return to their birth lines.

sentences.zh: 壬子，命太史監南宮說等於河南、北平地測日晷及極星，夏至日中立八尺之表，同時候之。

translations.literal: On renzi, Director of the Board of Astronomy Nangong Shuo and others were ordered to measure sundials and the pole star on the plains of Henan and Beiping; on the summer solstice an eight-foot gnomon was erected, and all observed simultaneously.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the court ordered Nangong Shuo, director of the Board of Astronomy, and others to measure sundials and the pole star on the Henan and Beiping plains; on the summer solstice they erected eight-foot gnomons and observed together.

sentences.zh: 陽城晷長一尺四寸八分弱，夜視北極出地高三十四度十分度之四；

translations.literal: At Yangcheng the shadow length was one chi, four cun, and eight fen minus a hair's breadth; at night the North Pole was seen rising thirty-four du and four tenths of a du above the horizon;
translations.idiomatic: At Yangcheng the shadow measured one chi, four cun, and eight fen less a fraction; at night the North Pole stood thirty-four and four-tenths du above the horizon;

sentences.zh: 浚儀岳台晷長一尺五寸微強，極高三十四度八分；

translations.literal: At the Yue Terrace in Junyi the shadow length was one chi and five cun plus a slight excess; the pole stood thirty-four du and eight fen high;
translations.idiomatic: At the Yue Terrace in Junyi the shadow was one chi and five cun plus a fraction; the pole stood thirty-four and eight fen du high;

sentences.zh: 南至朗州晷長七寸七分，極高二十九度半；

translations.literal: Going south to Lang Prefecture the shadow length was seven cun and seven fen; the pole stood twenty-nine and a half du high;
translations.idiomatic: Far south at Langzhou the shadow was seven cun and seven fen; the pole stood twenty-nine and a half du high;

sentences.zh: 北至蔚州，晷長二尺二寸九分，極高四十度。

translations.literal: Going north to Yu Prefecture, the shadow length was two chi, two cun, and nine fen; the pole stood forty du high.
translations.idiomatic: Far north at Yuzhou the shadow reached two chi, two cun, and nine fen; the pole stood forty du high.

sentences.zh: 南北相距三千六百八十八里九十步，晷差一尺五寸三分，極差十度半。

translations.literal: The north-south distance was three thousand six hundred eighty-eight li and ninety paces; the shadow differed by one chi, five cun, and three fen; the pole differed by ten and a half du.
translations.idiomatic: North and south were 3,688 li and ninety paces apart; shadow length differed by one chi, five cun, and three fen, and pole height by ten and a half du.

sentences.zh: 又南至交州，晷出表南三寸三分；

translations.literal: Further south to Jiao Prefecture, the shadow fell three cun and three fen south of the gnomon;
translations.idiomatic: Still farther south at Jiaozhou the shadow fell three cun and three fen south of the gnomon;

sentences.zh: 八月，海中南望老人星下，眾星粲然，皆古所未名，大率去南極二十度以上皆見。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, looking south over the sea beneath the Old Man Star, myriad stars shone brilliantly—all unnamed since antiquity; in general, stars more than twenty du from the South Pole were all visible.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, gazing south over the sea below the Old Man Star, they saw countless bright stars none had named before; in general, every star more than twenty du from the South Pole was visible.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁亥，停諸道按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dinghai, circuit investigation commissioners were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dinghai, the court abolished circuit investigation commissioners.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬辰，制聽逃戶自首，辟所在閒田，隨宜收稅，毋得差科征役，租庸一皆蠲免。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renchen, by edict fugitive households were permitted to turn themselves in; vacant lands wherever found were to be opened, with taxes levied as appropriate; no corvée or requisitions were to be assigned; rent and corvée taxes were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renchen, an edict allowed fugitive households to register; vacant land was to be opened and taxed as fit, with no corvée assignments, and all rent and corvée remitted.

sentences.zh: 仍以兵部員外郎兼侍御史宇文融為勸農使，巡行州縣，與吏民議定賦役。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong, Vice Director of the Ministry of War and concurrently Assistant Censor, was additionally made Agriculture Commissioner to tour prefectures and counties and consult with officials and people on fixing tax obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong, vice director of the Ministry of War and assistant censor, was named agriculture commissioner to tour the prefectures and settle tax obligations with officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 上以山東旱，命選台閣名臣以補刺史；

translations.literal: Because of drought in Shandong, the emperor ordered distinguished ministers from the central offices to be selected to fill prefectural posts;
translations.idiomatic: Because of drought in Shandong, Emperor Xuanzong ordered colonnade ministers chosen to serve as prefects;

sentences.zh: 壬午，以黃門侍郎王丘、中書侍郎長安崔沔、禮部侍郎、知制誥韓休等五人出為刺史。

translations.literal: On renwu, Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Wang Qiu, Vice Director of the Central Secretariat Cui Mian of Chang'an, Vice Director of Rites and Drafter of Edicts Han Xiu, and five others in all were sent out as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Vice Director Wang Qiu, Vice Director Cui Mian of Chang'an, Vice Director of Rites and drafter of edicts Han Xiu, and five others in all were sent out as prefects.

sentences.zh: 丘，同皎之從父兄子；

translations.literal: Qiu was the son of a paternal uncle of Tong Jiao;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu was a paternal cousin of Tong Jiao;

sentences.zh: 休，大敏之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiu was the grandson of Damin.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu was the grandson of Han Damin.

sentences.zh: 初，張說引崔沔為中書侍郎；

translations.literal: Initially, Zhang Yue brought in Cui Mian as Vice Director of the Central Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue had earlier brought Cui Mian in as vice director of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 故事，承宣制皆出宰相，侍郎署位而已。

translations.literal: By precedent, receiving and proclaiming edicts all came from the chancellor; the vice director merely affixed his name.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the chancellor alone drafted and proclaimed edicts; the vice director merely signed his name.

sentences.zh: 沔曰：「設官分職，上下相維，各申所見，事乃無失。

translations.literal: Mian said, "Offices are established and duties divided—superior and subordinate mutually support each other; each states his view, and affairs will be without error.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mian said, "Offices exist so that duties are divided and superiors and subordinates check one another; each should state his view, and business will not go wrong.

sentences.zh: 侍郎，令之貳也，豈得拱默而已！」

translations.literal: The vice director is the chancellor's second—how can he merely stand with folded hands in silence!"
translations.idiomatic: The vice director is the chancellor's deputy—how can he do nothing but stand silent!"

sentences.zh: 由是遇事多所異同，說不悅，故因是出之。

translations.literal: From this, on encountering affairs he often differed; Yue was displeased, and therefore on this pretext had him sent out.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he often dissented on policy; Zhang Yue was displeased and used this as grounds to have him sent out.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，突厥可汗遣其臣哥解頡利發來求婚。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Türk qaghan sent his subject Geli Fazha to come seeking marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, the Türk qaghan sent his minister Geli Fazha to sue for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 奚州蠻覃行璋反。

translations.literal: The Xi barbarian Tan Xingzhang of Xi Prefecture rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Xingzhang, a Xi chieftain in Xizhou, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 以監門衛大將軍楊思勖為黔中道招討使，將兵擊之。

translations.literal: Gate Guard General Yang Sixun was made Commissioner for Suppression and Pacification of the Qianzhong Circuit and led troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Gate Guard general Yang Sixun was made suppression commissioner for the Qianzhong circuit and marched against him.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，思勖生擒行璋，斬首三萬級而歸。

translations.literal: On guihai, Sixun captured Xingzhang alive, beheaded thirty thousand, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Yang Sixun took Xingzhang alive, claimed 30,000 heads, and returned.

sentences.zh: 加思勖輔國大將軍，俸祿、防閣皆依品給。

translations.literal: Sixun was promoted to Defender-General of the State; salary and guard of honor were all granted according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sixun was promoted to defender-general of the state, with salary and bodyguard allotments matched to rank.

sentences.zh: 赦行璋，以為洵水府別駕。

translations.literal: Xingzhang was pardoned and made vice-prefect of Xunshui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhang was pardoned and appointed vice-prefect of Xunshui.

sentences.zh: 姜皎既得罪，王皇后愈憂畏不安，然待下有恩，故無隨而譖之者，上猶豫不決者累歲。

translations.literal: After Jiang Jiao had fallen afoul of the law, Empress Wang grew ever more anxious and uneasy; yet she treated inferiors with kindness, so no one followed along to slander her; the emperor hesitated and could not decide—for years.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Jiao's disgrace Empress Wang grew more fearful, yet she treated her servants kindly, so none slandered her; Emperor Xuanzong hesitated for years.

sentences.zh: 後兄太子少保守一，以後無子，使僧明悟為後祭南北斗，剖霹靂木，書天地字及上名，合而佩之，祝曰：「佩此有子，當如則天皇后。」

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother, Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent Shouyi, because the empress had no son, had the monk Mingwu perform sacrifices for her to the Southern and Northern Dippers; he split thunderbolt wood, wrote the characters for Heaven and Earth and the emperor's name, joined them and had her wear them, praying, "Wearing this, if you have a son, may it be as with Empress Zetian."
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Shouyi, junior mentor to the heir, because the empress had no son, had the monk Mingwu sacrifice to the Southern and Northern Dippers for her; he split thunderbolt wood, wrote the characters for Heaven and Earth and the emperor's name, joined them as an amulet for her to wear, and prayed: "Wear this and bear a son, as Empress Wu did."

sentences.zh: 事覺，己卯，廢為庶人，移別室安置；

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, on jimao, she was deposed as commoner and moved to separate quarters for confinement;
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, on jimao she was deposed to commoner status and confined to separate quarters;

sentences.zh: 貶守一潭州別駕，中路賜死。

translations.literal: Shouyi was demoted to vice-prefect of Tan Prefecture and granted death en route.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was demoted to vice-prefect of Tanzhou and ordered to die on the road.

sentences.zh: 戶都尚書張嘉貞坐與守一交通，貶台州刺史。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Zhang Jiazhen, on account of communicating with Shouyi, was demoted to prefect of Tai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Zhang Jiazhen, for ties to Shouyi, was demoted to prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙申，突厥哥解頡利發還其國；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingshen, the Türk Geli Fazha returned to his country;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingshen, the Türk envoy Geli Fazha returned home;

sentences.zh: 以其使者輕，禮數不備，未許婚。

translations.literal: Because the envoy was disrespectful and ceremonial observances were incomplete, the marriage was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused the marriage alliance because the envoy was disrespectful and the ceremonial tribute insufficient.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以宇文融為御史中丞。

translations.literal: On jihai, Yuwen Rong was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Yuwen Rong was made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 融乘驛周流天下，事無大小，諸州先牒上勸農使，後申中書；

translations.literal: Rong rode post-horses and circulated throughout the realm; on matters great and small, all prefectures first reported to the Agriculture Commissioner, then memorialized the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong traveled the empire by post relay; on every matter, prefectures reported first to the agriculture commissioner and only then to the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 省司亦待融指摠，然後處決。

translations.literal: Central offices also waited for Rong's direction before deciding and executing.
translations.idiomatic: Central ministries waited for Yuwen Rong's instructions before acting.

sentences.zh: 時上將大攘四夷，急於用度，州縣畏融，多張虛數，凡得客戶八十餘萬，田亦稱是。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was about to greatly subdue the four barbarians and was urgent for revenue; prefectures and counties feared Rong and greatly inflated figures—altogether more than eight hundred thousand client households were registered, and fields matched accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was preparing for campaigns against the four frontiers and needed funds; prefectures feared Yuwen Rong and inflated their counts, registering more than 800,000 client households and matching fields.

sentences.zh: 歲終，增緡錢數百萬，悉進入宮；

translations.literal: At year's end, added cash revenue reached several million strings—all presented to the palace;
translations.idiomatic: By year's end added revenue reached several million strings of cash, all sent to the palace;

sentences.zh: 由是有寵。

translations.literal: From this he gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: From this he won imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 議者多言煩憂，不利百姓，上令集百寮於尚書省議之。

translations.literal: Critics widely said it was vexatious and harmful to the common people; the emperor ordered all officials gathered at the Department of State Affairs to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said the policy was oppressive and hurt the people; Emperor Xuanzong ordered the full bureaucracy to debate it at the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 公卿已下，畏融恩勢，皆不敢立異，惟戶部侍郎楊瑒抗議，以為：「括客免稅，不利居人。

translations.literal: From grand dukes down, all feared Rong's favor and power and dared not dissent; only Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Yang Chang protested, saying, "Registering client households and exempting them from tax is harmful to resident taxpayers.
translations.idiomatic: From the chief ministers down, all feared Yuwen Rong's influence and kept silent; only Vice Director Yang Chang objected: "Registering fugitives and exempting them from tax hurts those already on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 征籍外田稅，使百姓困弊，所得不補所失。」

translations.literal: Levying tax on fields outside the registers makes the common people exhausted; what is gained does not compensate for what is lost."
translations.idiomatic: Taxing unregistered land exhausts the people; the gains do not cover the losses."

sentences.zh: 未幾，瑒為華州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, Chang was made prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Chang was made prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以開府儀同三司宋璟為西京留守。

translations.literal: On renyin, Song Jing, Grand Master of Glorious Affairs with Imperial Pomp, was made regent of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Song Jing, Grand Master of Glorious Affairs with Imperial Pomp, was named regent of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，謝王特勒遣使入奏，稱「去年五月，金城公主遣使詣個失密國，雲欲走歸汝。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou, the Turgesh qaghan sent envoys to memorialize, stating, "Last May, Princess Jincheng sent envoys to the kingdom of Kabuli, saying she wished to flee back to you.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the tenth month's dingyou day, the Turgesh qaghan sent envoys to court reporting: "Last May Princess Jincheng sent envoys to Kabuli, saying she wished to flee back to you.

sentences.zh: 個失密王從臣國王借兵，共拒吐蕃。

translations.literal: The king of Kabuli, borrowing troops from his vassal kings, together resisted Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Kabuli borrowed troops from his vassal kings to resist the Tibetans together.

sentences.zh: 王遣臣入取進止。」

translations.literal: The king sent your subject to enter and receive instructions."
translations.idiomatic: The king sent me to ask what you command."

sentences.zh: 上以為然，賜帛遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct, bestowed silks, and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong approved, gave them silks, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 廢後王氏卒，後宮思慕後不已，上亦悔之。

translations.literal: The deposed Empress Wang died; the inner palace ceaselessly mourned the empress, and the emperor also regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed Empress Wang died, the inner palace mourned her endlessly, and Emperor Xuanzong regretted the deposition.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚午，上幸東都；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengwu, the emperor visited the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengwu, Emperor Xuanzong traveled to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 戊寅，至東都。

translations.literal: On wuyin, he reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，司徒申王摠薨，贈謚惠莊太子。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Situ Prince Shen Zong died; posthumously he was given the title Crown Prince Huihuang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Prince Shen Zong, Minister of Education, died and was posthumously titled Crown Prince Huihuang.

sentences.zh: 群臣屢上表請封禪，閏月，丁卯，制以明年十一月十日有事於泰山。

translations.literal: The ministers repeatedly submitted memorials requesting fengshan; in the intercalary month, on dingmao, by edict the ceremony at Mount Tai was set for the tenth day of the eleventh month of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers repeatedly petitioned for a fengshan; in the intercalary month, on dingmao, an edict fixed the Mount Tai rite for the tenth day of the eleventh month the following year.

sentences.zh: 時張說首建封禪之議，而源乾曜不欲為之，由是與說不平。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yue was the first to propose the fengshan plan, while Yuan Qianyao did not wish to undertake it; from this he and Yue were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue had been first to propose the fengshan, but Yuan Qianyao opposed it, and the two fell out.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹王李郁干卒，弟吐乾襲位。

translations.literal: That year, Khitan king Li Yigan died; his younger brother Tugan succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Khitan king Li Yigan died and his brother Tugan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，庚申，以御史中丞宇文融兼戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on gengshen, Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong was made concurrently Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the second month's gengshen day, censor-in-chief Yuwen Rong was also made vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 制以所得客戶稅錢均充所在常平倉本；

translations.literal: By edict the tax revenue from registered client households was evenly applied as seed capital for local Ever-Normal Granaries;
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that client household tax revenue fund local Ever-Normal Granaries;

sentences.zh: 又委使司與州縣議作勸農社，使貧富相恤，耕耘以時。

translations.literal: The commissioner's office was further entrusted with prefectures and counties to deliberate establishing agricultural encouragement associations, so that rich and poor might aid each other and plow and sow in season.
translations.idiomatic: And charged commissioners and prefectures to organize farming cooperatives so rich and poor could help one another and sow on time.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，更命長從宿衛之士曰「擴騎」，分隸十二衛，總十二萬人為六番。

translations.literal: On yihai, the long-service palace guards were renamed "Expanded Cavalry," assigned to the twelve guards, totaling one hundred twenty thousand men in six rotations.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the long-service guards were renamed the Expanded Cavalry, assigned to the twelve guards—120,000 men in six rotations.

sentences.zh: 上自選諸司長官有聲望者大理卿源光裕、尚書左丞楊承令、兵部侍郎寇泚等十一人為刺史，命宰相、諸王及諸司長官、台郎、御史餞於洛濱，供張甚盛。

translations.literal: The emperor personally selected eleven men of reputation among department chiefs—Minister of Justice Yuan Guangyu, Left Vice Director Yang Chengling, Vice Director of War Kou Ci, and others—as prefects; he ordered chancellors, princes, department chiefs, secretariat and censorate officers to host a farewell feast on the Luo River bank—the provisioning was very lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong personally chose eleven distinguished department chiefs—including Minister of Justice Yuan Guangyu, Vice Director Yang Chengling, and Vice Director of War Kou Ci—as prefects, and ordered chancellors, princes, officials, and censors to give them a lavish farewell feast on the Luo River bank.

sentences.zh: 賜以御膳，太常具樂，內坊歌妓；

translations.literal: They were granted imperial banquets; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices provided music; inner-palace singing girls performed;
translations.idiomatic: They were given imperial feasts, music from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and palace singers;

sentences.zh: 上自書十韻詩，命將軍高力士賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote a ten-rhyme poem and ordered General Gao Lishi to bestow it on them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong wrote a ten-rhyme poem and had General Gao Lishi present it to them.

sentences.zh: 光裕，乾曜之從孫也。

translations.literal: Guangyu was the grand-nephew of Qianyao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Guangyu was the grand-nephew of Yuan Qianyao.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲午，太子嗣謙更名鴻；

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiawu, Heir Apparent Suiqian was renamed Hong;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu, Heir Apparent Suiqian was renamed Hong;

sentences.zh: 徙郯王嗣直為慶王，更名潭；

translations.literal: Prince of Tan Suiqi was moved to Prince of Qing and renamed Tan;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Tan Suiqi became Prince of Qing and was renamed Tan;

sentences.zh: 陝王嗣升為忠王，更名浚；

translations.literal: Prince of Shan Suisheng was made Prince of Zhong and renamed Jun;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shan Suisheng was made Prince of Zhong and renamed Jun;

sentences.zh: 鄂王嗣真為棣王，更名洽；

translations.literal: Prince of E Suizhen was made Prince of Di and renamed Qia;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of E Suizhen was made Prince of Di and renamed Qia;

sentences.zh: 鄂王嗣初更名涓；

translations.literal: Prince of E Suichu was renamed Juan;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of E Suichu was renamed Juan;

sentences.zh: 鄄王嗣玄為榮王，更名滉。

translations.literal: Prince of Juan Suixuan was made Prince of Rong and renamed Huang;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Juan Suixuan was made Prince of Rong and renamed Huang;

sentences.zh: 又立子涺為光王，濰為儀王，沄為穎王，澤為永王，清為壽王，洄為延王，沐為盛王，溢為濟王。

translations.literal: Additionally the sons Li, Wei, Yun, Ze, Qing, Hui, Mu, and Yi were established as Princes of Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Shou, Yan, Sheng, and Ji respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Eight more sons were created princes: Li as Guang, Wei as Yi, Yun as Ying, Ze as Yong, Qing as Shou, Hui as Yan, Mu as Sheng, and Yi as Ji.

sentences.zh: 丙申，御史大夫程行湛奏：「周朝酷吏來俊臣等二十三人，情狀尤重，子孫請皆禁錮；

translations.literal: On bingshen, Censor-in-Chief Cheng Xingchen memorialized: "The Zhou dynasty's cruel officials Lai Junchen and twenty-two others—their circumstances were especially grave; their descendants should all be confined and barred;
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Censor-in-Chief Cheng Xingchen memorialized: "The Zhou dynasty's cruel officials Lai Junchen and twenty-two others of the gravest guilt—their descendants should all be barred from office;

sentences.zh: 傅遊藝等四人差輕，子孫不聽近任。」

translations.literal: Fu Youyi and four others were somewhat lighter—their descendants are forbidden from serving in nearby posts."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youyi and four others were lesser cases—their descendants may not hold posts near the capital."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 汾州刺史楊承令不欲外補，意怏怏，自言：「吾出守有由。」

translations.literal: Fen Prefecture Prefect Yang Chengling did not wish to serve outside the capital; he was displeased and said to himself, "There is a reason for my being sent out to govern."
translations.idiomatic: Fenzhou prefect Yang Chengling resented his provincial assignment and muttered, "There is a reason I was sent out."

sentences.zh: 上聞之，怒，壬寅，貶睦州別駕。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he was angry; on renyin, [Chengling] was demoted to vice-prefect of Mu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong heard, he was furious; on renyin Yang Chengling was demoted to vice-prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 張說草封禪儀獻之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue drafted the fengshan ceremony and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue drafted the Mount Tai fengshan rites and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙辰，上與中書門下及禮官、學士宴於集仙殿。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingchen, the emperor feasted with the Chancellery, the Secretariat, rites officials, and academicians in the Hall of Assembled Immortals.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingchen, Emperor Xuanzong gave a banquet in the Hall of Assembled Immortals for the chancellors, the Secretariat, rites officials, and academicians.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「仙者憑虛之論，朕所不取。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Immortals are talk of emptiness—what I do not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Talk of immortals is idle speculation, and I will have none of it.

sentences.zh: 賢者濟理之具，朕今與卿曹合宴，宜更名曰集賢殿。」

translations.literal: Worthies are the means to aid governance; I now feast with you all—it should be renamed the Hall of Assembled Worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Worthies are what aid good government; since I feast with you today, this hall should be renamed the Hall of Assembled Worthies."

sentences.zh: 其書院官五品以上為學士，六品以下為直學士；

translations.literal: Its academy officials of the fifth rank and above were made academicians, those of the sixth rank and below were made direct academicians;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the academy at fifth rank and above were styled academicians; those of sixth rank and below, direct academicians.

sentences.zh: 以張說知院事，右散騎常侍徐堅副之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue was put in charge of the academy, with Right Regular Attendant Xu Jian as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue was made director of the academy, with Xu Jian, Right Regular Attendant, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 上欲以說為大學士，說固辭而止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Yue Grand Academician; Yue firmly declined and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to name Zhang Yue Grand Academician, but Zhang Yue steadfastly refused and the appointment went no further.

sentences.zh: 說以大駕東巡，恐突厥乘間入寇，議加兵守邊，召兵部郎中裴光庭謀之。

translations.literal: Yue, because the great carriage would tour east, feared the Türk would seize the interval to invade; he discussed increasing troops to guard the border and summoned Bureau Director of the Ministry of War Pei Guangting to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the imperial tour was heading east, Zhang Yue feared the Türk might seize the moment to raid the frontier; he proposed reinforcing the border garrisons and summoned Pei Guangting, a director in the Ministry of War, to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 光庭曰：「封禪者，告成功也。

translations.literal: Guangting said, "Fengshan is announcing success.
