translations.idiomatic: Guangting said, "The fengshan rite announces success to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今將升中於天，而戎狄是懼，非所以昭盛德也。」

translations.literal: Now about to ascend the central peak to Heaven, yet the Rong and Di are feared—this is not the way to display abundant virtue."
translations.idiomatic: You are about to ascend Mount Tai to report to Heaven, yet you fear the barbarians—that is hardly how one displays great virtue."

sentences.zh: 說曰：「然則若之何？」

translations.literal: Yue said, "Then what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue asked, "Then what should we do?"

sentences.zh: 光庭曰：「四夷之中，突厥為大，比屢求和親，而朝遷羈縻，未決許也。

translations.literal: Guangting said, "Among the four barbarians, the Türk is greatest; recently they have repeatedly sought marriage alliance, yet the court has delayed with tied-and-reined policy and has not decided to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting said, "Of the four quarters the Türk is the greatest; they have repeatedly sought a marriage alliance, yet the court has kept them on a loose tether and never granted it.

sentences.zh: 今遣一使，征其大臣從封泰山，彼必欣然承命；

translations.literal: Now send one envoy and summon their chief minister to follow the fengshan at Mount Tai—they will surely gladly accept the order;
translations.idiomatic: Send an envoy now and invite their chief minister to attend the Mount Tai fengshan—they will gladly accept;

sentences.zh: 突厥來，則戎狄君長無不皆來。

translations.literal: When the Türk come, then none of the Rong and Di lords will fail to come.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Türk come, every other barbarian chief will follow.

sentences.zh: 可以偃旗臥鼓，高枕有餘矣。」

translations.literal: One can lower banners and lay drums aside, and rest on a high pillow with plenty to spare."
translations.idiomatic: Then you may lower the banners, stow the drums, and sleep easy."

sentences.zh: 說曰「善！

translations.literal: Yue said, "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 說所不及。」

translations.literal: What Yue had not reached."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond what Zhang Yue had thought of."

sentences.zh: 即奏行之。

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the plan at once and it was adopted.

sentences.zh: 光庭，行儉之子也。

translations.literal: Guangting was the son of Xingjian.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting was a son of Pei Xingjian.

sentences.zh: 上遣中書直省袁振攝鴻臚卿，諭旨於突厥，小殺與闕特勒、暾欲谷環坐帳中，置酒，謂振曰：「吐蕃，狗種；

translations.literal: The emperor sent Secretariat Direct Office staff Yuan Zhen as acting Master of Banquets to convey the purpose to the Türk; Xiaosha with Kue Tegin and Ton Yabghu sat in a circle in the tent, wine was set out, and he said to Zhen, "Tibet—dog breed;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yuan Zhen of the Secretariat Direct Office to serve as acting Master of Banquets and convey the imperial message to the Türk. Xiaosha sat with Kue Tegin and Ton Yabghu in a circle inside the tent over wine and said to Yuan Zhen, "The Tibetans are a dog breed;

sentences.zh: 奚、契丹，本突厥奴也；

translations.literal: Xi and Khitan were originally Türk slaves;
translations.idiomatic: the Xi and Khitan were once Türk slaves;

sentences.zh: 皆得尚主。

translations.literal: All obtained marriage with imperial princesses.
translations.idiomatic: yet all were given imperial princesses in marriage.

sentences.zh: 突厥前後求婚獨不許，何也？

translations.literal: The Türk before and after sought marriage yet alone were not granted—why?
translations.idiomatic: The Türk have asked for marriage again and again, yet alone we are refused—why?

sentences.zh: 且吾亦知入蕃公主皆非天子女，今豈問真偽！

translations.literal: Moreover I also know the princesses who entered Fan lands were none daughters of Heaven—now why question true or false!
translations.idiomatic: And I know perfectly well that none of the princesses sent to foreign courts were the emperor's own daughters—why quibble over authenticity now!

sentences.zh: 但屢請不獲，愧見諸蕃耳。」

translations.literal: Only having repeatedly requested without obtaining, ashamed to face the various Fan."
translations.idiomatic: I am simply ashamed to face the other tribes after pleading so often in vain."

sentences.zh: 振許為之奏請。

translations.literal: Zhen promised to memorialize the request for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen promised to memorialize the request on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 小殺乃使其大臣阿史德頡利發入貢，因扈從東巡。

translations.literal: Xiaosha thereupon sent his chief minister Ashide Bilifa to bring tribute and thereby escort on the eastern tour.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosha then sent his minister Ashide Bilifa to pay tribute and accompany the eastern tour.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚寅，妖賊劉定高帥眾夜犯通洛門；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengyin, demonic bandit Liu Dinggao led a crowd by night to attack Tongluo Gate;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengyin, the sorcerer-rebel Liu Dinggao led his followers in a night attack on Tongluo Gate;

sentences.zh: 悉捕斬之。

translations.literal: All were captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: They were all captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，張說議封禪儀，請以睿宗配皇地祇；

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Zhang Yue discussed the fengshan ceremony and requested that Ruizong be paired with Imperial Earth Lord;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Zhang Yue set out the fengshan rites and proposed that Emperor Ruizong accompany Imperial Earth at the rite;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙戌，上謂宰臣曰：「《春秋》不書祥瑞，惟記有年。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingxu, the emperor said to the chief ministers, "The Spring and Autumn Annals does not record auspicious omens—only records years of plenty."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingxu, Emperor Xuanzong told the chief ministers, "The Spring and Autumn Annals records no auspicious portents—only good harvests."

sentences.zh: 敕自今州縣毋得更奏祥瑞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from now on prefectures and counties must not again memorialize auspicious omens.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that prefectures and counties cease reporting auspicious omens.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸丑，作水運渾天成，上具列宿，注水激輪，令其自轉，晝夜一週。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guichou, a water-driven armillary sphere of the heavens was made; above it had the arrayed lodges; water was poured in to drive the wheel, making it turn by itself, one circuit day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guichou, the court built a water-powered armillary sphere of the heavens crowned with the constellations; poured water drove the wheel so that it turned on its own, completing one revolution each day and night.

sentences.zh: 別置二輪，絡在天外，綴以日月，逆天而行，淹速合度。

translations.literal: Separately two wheels were placed, linked outside heaven, adorned with sun and moon, moving contrary to heaven, fast and slow matching degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Two additional wheels were mounted beyond the sphere and fitted with models of the sun and moon, turning against the heavens at speeds calibrated to their proper motion.

sentences.zh: 置木匱為地平，令儀半在地下，又立二木人，每刻擊鼓，每辰擊鐘，機械皆藏匱中。

translations.literal: A wooden chest was set as the level of earth, making the instrument half below ground; two wooden men were also erected, beating a drum each quarter-hour and a bell each double-hour—all mechanisms hidden in the chest.
translations.idiomatic: A wooden casing served as the horizon, half the instrument lying below ground level; two wooden figures were erected to strike a drum each quarter-hour and a bell each double-hour, all the machinery concealed within the casing.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，車駕發東都，百官、貴戚、四夷酋長從行。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the imperial carriage set out from the Eastern Capital; the hundred officials, noble kin, and chieftains of the four barbarians followed in the procession.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the imperial procession left the Eastern Capital, accompanied by officials, imperial relatives, and chieftains from the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 每置頓，數十里中人畜被野；

translations.literal: At each halt, for several tens of li men and livestock covered the wilds;
translations.idiomatic: At every stop for the night, men and livestock carpeted the countryside for miles;

sentences.zh: 有司輦載供具之物，數百里不絕。

translations.literal: The responsible offices carried supplies on litters—the line stretched for several hundred li without break.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' carriers hauling provisions stretched unbroken for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙戌，至泰山下，己丑，上備法駕，至山下，御馬登山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingxu, they reached the foot of Mount Tai; on jichou, the emperor prepared the legal carriage, reached the foot of the mountain, and rode a horse up the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingxu, they reached Mount Tai; on jichou Emperor Xuanzong took the full imperial equipage to the foot of the mountain and rode up on horseback.

sentences.zh: 留從官於谷口，獨與宰相及祠官俱登，儀衛環列於山下百餘里。

translations.literal: Retaining the attendant officials at the valley mouth, he alone with the chief ministers and sacrifice officials ascended together; ceremonial guards encircled and lined the foot of the mountain for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He left the entourage at the valley mouth and ascended only with the chief ministers and ritual officers, while guard formations ringed the mountain for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 上問禮部侍郎賀知章曰：「前代玉牒之文，何故秘之？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Vice Minister of Rites He Zhizhang, "Why were the jade-tablet texts of former ages kept secret?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked He Zhizhang, Vice Minister of Rites, "Why were the texts inscribed on the jade tablets kept secret in past ages?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「或密求神仙，故不欲人見。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Perhaps secretly seeking immortals, therefore not wishing people to see."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Some emperors sought immortality in secret and did not want others to read them."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾為蒼生祈福耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I only pray blessing for the black-haired people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I seek blessings only for the common people."

sentences.zh: 乃出玉牒，宣示群臣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the jade tablet was produced and shown to explain to the hundred ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He then displayed the jade tablet and read its text aloud to the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，上祀昊天上帝於山上，群臣祀五帝百神於山下之壇；

translations.literal: On gengyin, the emperor sacrificed to August Heaven Lord on the mountain; the hundred ministers sacrificed to the Five Emperors and the hundred spirits at the altar below the mountain;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Emperor Xuanzong sacrificed to August Heaven on the summit, while the ministers offered to the Five Emperors and the myriad spirits at the altar below;

sentences.zh: 其餘仿乾封故事。

translations.literal: The rest followed the precedent of the Qianfeng era.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining ceremonies followed the precedents of the Qianfeng fengshan of 666.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，祭皇地祇於社首。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Imperial Earth Lord was sacrificed to at Sheshou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he sacrificed to Imperial Earth at Sheshou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，上御帳殿，受朝覲，赦天下，封泰山神為天齊王，禮秩加三公一等。

translations.literal: On renchen, the emperor occupied the tent-palace, received court audience, pardoned all under Heaven, enfeoffed the Mount Tai spirit as King Tianqi, ceremonial rank one grade above the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he held court in the tent-palace, received homage, pardoned the empire, and enfeoffed the spirit of Mount Tai as King Tianqi with ceremonial rank one grade above the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 張說多引兩省吏及以所親攝官登山。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue largely brought Chancellery and Secretariat clerks and used his own favorites as acting officials to ascend the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue brought many clerks from the two secretariats and numerous personal appointees up the mountain with him.

sentences.zh: 禮畢推恩，往往加階超入五品而不及百官；

translations.literal: When the rites were finished he extended grace; often ranks were raised skipping into the fifth rank without reaching the hundred officials;
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he distributed favor: many were promoted straight into fifth rank while the regular officials were passed over;

sentences.zh: 中書舍人張九齡諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafting Officer Zhang Jiuling remonstrated; [the emperor] did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling, a drafting officer of the Secretariat, remonstrated in vain.

sentences.zh: 又，扈從士卒，但加勳而無賜物，由是中外怨之。

translations.literal: Further, the escort soldiers received only added merit without gift goods; thereby inside and outside resented this.
translations.idiomatic: The escort troops received only merit citations and no gifts, and resentment spread through court and camp alike.

sentences.zh: 初，隋末，國馬皆為盜賊及戎狄所掠，唐初才得牝牡三千匹於赤岸澤，徙之隴右，命太僕張萬歲掌之。

translations.literal: Initially, at the end of Sui, state horses were all plundered by bandits and Rong and Di; at the beginning of Tang only three thousand mares and stallions were obtained at Chianze Marsh, moved to Longyou, and Grand Master of the Stud Zhang Wansui was ordered to manage them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, bandits and barbarians had carried off nearly every state horse; early Tang recovered only three thousand broodmares and stallions from Chianze Marsh and moved them to Longyou under Grand Master of the Stud Zhang Wansui.

sentences.zh: 萬歲善於其職，自貞觀至麟德，馬蕃息及七十萬匹，分為八坊、四十八監，各置使以領之。

translations.literal: Wansui was good at his post; from Zhenguan to Longde horses multiplied to seven hundred thousand, divided into eight wards and forty-eight pastures, each with a commissioner placed to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Wansui excelled in the post; from the Zhenguan era to Longde the herds grew to seven hundred thousand head, organized into eight wards and forty-eight pastures each under its own commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時天下以一縑易一馬。

translations.literal: At that time all under Heaven exchanged one bolt of silk for one horse.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a bolt of silk could buy a horse anywhere in the realm.

sentences.zh: 垂拱以後，馬潛耗太半。

translations.literal: After Chuigong, horses secretly dwindled by more than half.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chuigong era the herds quietly dwindled by more than half.

sentences.zh: 上初即位，牧馬有二十四萬匹，以太僕卿王毛仲為內外閒廄使，少卿張景順副之。

translations.literal: When the emperor first ascended the throne, pastured horses numbered two hundred forty thousand; Grand Master of the Stud Wang Maochong was made commissioner of inner and outer stud farms, Vice Master Zhang Jingshun as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong first took the throne there were two hundred forty thousand pastured horses; he made Grand Master of the Stud Wang Maochong commissioner of the inner and outer stud farms, with Vice Master Zhang Jingshun as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 至是有馬四十三萬匹，牛羊稱是。

translations.literal: By now there were four hundred thirty thousand horses, cattle and sheep commensurately.
translations.idiomatic: By now the herds had grown to four hundred thirty thousand horses, with cattle and sheep in proportion.

sentences.zh: 上之東封，以牧馬數萬匹從，色別為群，望之如雲錦。

translations.literal: The emperor's eastern fengshan—several ten-thousands of pastured horses followed, grouped by color, gazing upon them like cloud brocade.
translations.idiomatic: For the eastern fengshan tens of thousands of pastured horses followed, grouped by color—a spectacle like brocade clouds on the plain.

sentences.zh: 上嘉毛仲之功，癸巳，加毛仲開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Maochong's achievement; on guisi Maochong was promoted to Grand Master Consultant with the Same Rank as the Three Excellencies with the Opening of a Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Wang Maochong's achievement; on guisi he was promoted to Grand Master Consultant, Honorary Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 甲午，車駕發泰山；

translations.literal: On jiawu, the imperial carriage set out from Mount Tai;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the imperial procession left Mount Tai;

sentences.zh: 庚申，幸孔子宅致祭。

translations.literal: On gengshen, [the emperor] visited Confucius's dwelling and performed sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: on gengshen he visited Confucius's residence and offered sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 上還，至宋州，宴從官於樓上，刺史寇泚預焉。

translations.literal: The emperor returned; reaching Song Prefecture, he feasted the attendant officials on a tower; Prefect Kou Ci was among them.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey Emperor Xuanzong reached Song Prefecture and feasted his entourage on a pavilion; Prefect Kou Ci was present.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，上謂張說曰：「向者屢遣使臣分巡諸道，察吏善惡，今因封禪歷諸州，乃知使臣負我多矣。

translations.literal: When wine was warm, the emperor said to Zhang Yue, "Before I repeatedly sent envoys to tour the various circuits separately, inspecting officials' good and evil; now because of fengshan passing through the various prefectures, I know the envoys failed me greatly.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed, the emperor said to Zhang Yue, "I have often sent commissioners to tour the circuits and report on local officials. Passing through these prefectures on the fengshan tour, I see how badly those commissioners have misled me.

sentences.zh: 懷州刺史王丘，餼牽之外，一無他獻。

translations.literal: Huai Prefecture Prefect Wang Qiu, beyond gifts of sheep and cattle, had nothing else presented.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu, prefect of Huai Prefecture, brought nothing beyond the prescribed sheep and cattle.

sentences.zh: 魏州刺史崔沔，供張無錦繡，示我以儉。

translations.literal: Wei Prefecture Prefect Cui Yong, provisions without brocade and embroidery, showed me his frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yong of Wei Prefecture offered no brocade or embroidery in his supplies—he showed me thrift.

sentences.zh: 濟州刺史斐耀卿，表數百言，莫非規諫，且曰：『人或重擾，則不足以告成。』

translations.literal: Ji Prefecture Prefect Pei Yaoqing's memorial of several hundred words—none not admonition; moreover saying, 'If people are heavily harassed, then it is not enough to announce success.'
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoqing of Ji Prefecture sent a memorial of several hundred words, every line admonition; he wrote, 'If the people are badly burdened, success cannot truly be proclaimed to Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 朕常置之坐隅，且以戒左右。

translations.literal: I always place it at the corner of my seat, and thereby admonish those at my side.
translations.idiomatic: I keep that memorial at my elbow to remind those around me.

sentences.zh: 如三人者，不勞人以市恩，真良吏矣！」

translations.literal: Such as these three men—not troubling people to buy favor—truly good officials!"
translations.idiomatic: Men like these three ask nothing of the people to buy favor—they are true good officials!"

sentences.zh: 顧謂寇泚曰：「比亦屢有以酒饌不豐訴於朕者，知卿不借譽於左右也。」

translations.literal: Turning he said to Kou Ci, "Recently there have also repeatedly been those who complained to me that wine and food were not abundant—I know you did not borrow praise from those at my side."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Kou Ci he said, "Others have complained to me that the feast here was too plain—I know you did not urge my attendants to praise you."

sentences.zh: 自舉酒賜之。

translations.literal: He himself raised wine and granted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his cup and offered Kou Ci a drink from his own hand.

sentences.zh: 宰臣帥群臣起賀，樓上皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The chief ministers led the hundred ministers to rise in congratulation; on the tower all called ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers led the court in congratulations, and the pavilion rang with cries of "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 由是以丘為尚書左丞，沔為散騎侍郎，耀卿為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereby Qiu was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yong Regular Attendant of the Right, Yaoqing Prefect of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu was thereupon made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, Cui Yong Regular Attendant of the Right, and Pei Yaoqing prefect of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 耀卿，叔業之七世孫也。

translations.literal: Yaoqing was the seventh-generation descendant of Shuye.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoqing was a seventh-generation descendant of Pei Shuye.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙巳，還東都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yisi, [they] returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yisi, the emperor returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利發辭歸，上厚賜而遣之，竟不許婚。

translations.literal: Türk Bilifa took leave to return; the emperor richly rewarded and sent him off, yet in the end did not grant marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ashide Bilifa of the Türk took leave to return home; the emperor showered gifts on him and sent him off, but never granted the marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 王毛仲有寵於上，百官附之者輻湊。

translations.literal: Wang Maochong had favor with the emperor; the hundred officials who attached to him gathered like wheel spokes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maochong enjoyed the emperor's favor, and officials flocked to his side.

sentences.zh: 毛仲嫁女，上問何須。

translations.literal: Maochong was marrying off his daughter; the emperor asked what he still needed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Maochong was marrying off his daughter, the emperor asked what he still lacked.

sentences.zh: 毛仲頓首對曰：「臣萬事已備，但未得客。」

translations.literal: Maochong kowtowed and replied, "Your subject's ten thousand affairs are all prepared, but I have not yet obtained guests."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maochong kowtowed and said, "Your servant has arranged everything—except guests."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「張說、源乾曜輩豈不可呼邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Zhang Yue, Yuan Qianyao and the like—cannot they be summoned?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Cannot men like Zhang Yue and Yuan Qianyao be summoned?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此則得之。」

translations.literal: He replied, "These I can obtain."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Those I can get."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「知汝所不能致者一人耳，必宋璟也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I know the one person you cannot bring—it must be Song Jing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know there is one man you cannot bring—and that must be Song Jing."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「然。」

translations.literal: He replied, "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Exactly so."

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「朕明日為汝召客。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "Tomorrow I will summon guests for you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Tomorrow I shall summon your guests for you."

sentences.zh: 明日，上謂宰相：「朕奴毛仲有婚事，卿等宜與諸達官悉詣其第。」

translations.literal: The next day the emperor said to the chief ministers, "My servant Maochong has a marriage affair—you should with all eminent officials completely go to his residence."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the chief ministers, "My servant Maochong is holding a wedding—you and all the senior officials should attend his house."

sentences.zh: 既而日中，眾客未敢舉箸，待璟。

translations.literal: Presently midday came; the many guests did not dare raise chopsticks, waiting for Jing.
translations.idiomatic: By midday the guests had not dared touch their food, waiting for Song Jing.

sentences.zh: 久之，方至，先執酒西向拜謝，飲不盡卮，遽稱腹痛而歸。

translations.literal: After long time he finally arrived; first taking wine he bowed facing west in thanks, drank without finishing the cup, suddenly claimed belly pain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At last Song Jing arrived; he raised a cup, bowed westward in apology, drank without finishing, then abruptly pleaded stomach pain and left.

sentences.zh: 璟之剛直，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: Jing's firm uprightness—old yet more steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing's integrity only hardened with age.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹王李吐乾與可突干復相猜忌，攜公主來奔，不敢復還，更封遼陽王，留宿衛；

translations.literal: Before this, Khitan king Li Tugan and Ketugan again mutually suspected each other; he brought the princess and came to flee, dared not return again, was again enfeoffed King of Liaoyang, kept in palace guard;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitan king Li Tugan and Ketugan had grown mutually suspicious; Tugan fled to court with the princess given him in marriage, dared not return, was re-enfeoffed as King of Liaoyang, and kept on palace guard duty;

sentences.zh: 可突干立李盡忠之弟邵固為主。

translations.literal: Ketugan installed Li Jinzhong's younger brother Shaogu as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Ketugan installed Shaogu, younger brother of Li Jinzhong, as khagan.

sentences.zh: 車駕東巡，邵固詣行在，因從至泰山，拜左羽林大將軍、靜折軍經略大使。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage toured east; Shaogu went to the traveling palace and thereby followed to Mount Tai, was appointed Left General of the Feathered Forest and commissioner for the Jingzhe Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern tour Shaogu came to the imperial camp, followed the procession to Mount Tai, and was appointed Left General of the Feathered Forest and commissioner for the Jingzhe Army.

sentences.zh: 上疑吏部選試不公，時選期已迫，御史中丞宇文融密奏，請分吏部為十銓。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected the Ministry of Personnel selection examinations were unfair; the selection period was already pressing; Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong secretly memorialized, requesting the Ministry of Personnel be divided into ten selection boards.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong suspected bias in the Ministry of Personnel examinations; with the selection deadline near, Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong secretly proposed splitting the ministry into ten selection boards.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以禮部尚書蘇頲等十人掌吏部選，試判將畢，遽召入禁中決定，吏部尚書、侍郎皆不得預。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Minister of Rites Su Ting and nine others—ten men—were put in charge of Ministry of Personnel selection; when the examination judgments were nearly finished, they were suddenly summoned into the inner palace to decide; the Minister and Vice Ministers of Personnel were both not permitted to participate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Su Ting, Minister of Rites, and nine others—ten men in all—took charge of personnel selection; when the written examinations were nearly done they were summoned into the palace to decide appointments, and the minister and vice ministers of Personnel were excluded.

sentences.zh: 左遮子吳兢上表，以為：「陛下曲受讒言，不信有司，非居上臨人推誠感物之道。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Officer Wu Jing submitted a memorial, holding that: "Your Majesty bends to accept slander, does not trust the responsible offices—this is not the Way of occupying the high place and facing people, extending sincerity to move things.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Officer Wu Jing memorialized: "Your Majesty has heedlessly accepted slander and lost faith in the responsible offices—that is not how a ruler above others wins loyalty through sincerity.

sentences.zh: 昔陳平、邴吉，漢之宰相，尚不對錢谷之數，不問斗死之人；

translations.literal: Formerly Chen Ping and Bing Ji, Han chief ministers, still did not answer numbers of money and grain, did not inquire about persons dead by the peck-measure;
translations.idiomatic: Even Chen Ping and Bing Ji, chancellors of Han, would not tally tax receipts or ask how many people died of famine in the fields;

sentences.zh: 況大唐萬乘之君，豈得下行銓選之事乎？

translations.literal: How much more the lord of ten thousand chariots of Great Tang—how can he descend to conduct selection affairs?
translations.idiomatic: how much less should the sovereign of Great Tang descend to grading examination papers?

sentences.zh: 凡選人書判，並請委之有司，停此十銓。」

translations.literal: All candidates' written judgments—please altogether entrust to the responsible offices; stop these ten selection boards."
translations.idiomatic: Leave all candidates' written examinations to the proper offices and abolish these ten boards."

sentences.zh: 上雖不即從，明年復故。

translations.literal: Although the emperor did not immediately follow, the next year restored the former arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree at once, but the following year the old system was restored.

sentences.zh: 是歲，東都斗米十五錢，青、齊五錢，粟三錢。

translations.literal: That year, in the Eastern Capital a dou of rice was fifteen cash; in Qing and Qi, five cash; millet, three cash.
translations.idiomatic: That year rice in the Eastern Capital sold for fifteen cash per dou; in Qing and Qi prefectures, five cash; millet, three cash.

sentences.zh: 于闐王尉遲眺陰結突厥及諸胡謀叛，安西副大都護杜暹發兵捕斬之，更為立王。

translations.literal: The king of Khotan, Yuchi Tiao, secretly joined with the Türks and various Hu peoples in plotting rebellion; the Assistant Protector-General of Anxi Du Xian sent troops, captured and executed him, and installed a new king.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Tiao, king of Khotan, secretly conspired with the Türks and other frontier peoples to rebel; Du Xian, deputy protector-general of Anxi, marched against him, executed him, and set up a new king.
